options.B: A complex or changing operating environment.
options.C: Multiple locations with similar operations.
options.D: Subsequent engagements to provide assurance about inventory performed at the same location.

question: Field work is a systematic process of objectively gathering information about an entity’s operations, evaluating it, and determining whether those operations meet acceptable standards. Which of the following is part of the work performed before field work begins?

options.A: Expanding or altering engagement procedures if circumstances warrant.
options.B: Applying the engagement work program to accomplish engagement objectives.
options.C: Creating workpapers that document the engagement.
options.D: Developing a written engagement work program.

question: The action taken by an internal auditor who discovers a significant area not included in the engagement work program should be to

options.A: Evaluate whether completion of the engagement as planned will be adequate.
options.B: Perform the additional work deemed necessary without regard to the additional time needed to complete the engagement.
options.C: Continue the engagement as planned and include the unforeseen area in a subsequent engagement.
options.D: Document the finding in the workpapers and take no further action until instructed to do so.

question: An internal auditing supervisor reviewed the system of controls and the organizational objective of the purchasing department. What facet of engagement planning was the supervisor developing?

options.A: Internal auditing policy manual.
options.B: Engagement work schedule.
options.C: Engagement work program.
options.D: Internal auditing budget.

question: An internal auditor determines that actual procedures differ from prescribed control procedures. The internal auditor should

options.A: Require operating personnel to conform to prescribed procedures.
options.B: Expand all aspects of the engagement to determine other differences from prescribed procedures.
options.C: Postpone the engagement work program until management has addressed the issue.
options.D: Document the discrepancies and make any appropriate recommendations to management.

question: Which of the following are typically included in an engagement work program?

options.A: Engagement objectives, preliminary survey, technical requirements, and procedures.
options.B: Engagement objectives, technical requirements, procedures, and workpapers.
options.C: Technical requirements, nature of testing, procedures, and preliminary conclusion.
options.D: Engagement objectives, technical requirements, nature of testing, and procedures.

question: When preparing for an engagement, the audit team lacks sufficient detail for the criteria against which objectives are to be evaluated. Which step is most appropriate to resolve this deficiency?

options.A: Develop the criteria internally and distribute among the team.
options.B: Consult with stakeholders involved to gain insights and clarity.
options.C: Use broad criteria to maintain flexibility.
options.D: Continue without detailed criteria and adjust as needed during the audit.

question: In a meeting with the board, the CAE presents findings that suggest potential noncompliance with data protection regulations. What should be the recommended action plan for the organization to address these compliance issues urgently?

options.A: Perform a detailed compliance audit with special focus on data privacy.
options.B: Implement immediate technical fixes to secure data systems.
options.C: Advise on legal consultations to manage potential violations.
options.D: Outline a strategic plan to integrate data compliance measures into daily operations.

question: An organization plans to upgrade its accounting software to improve efficiency and data accuracy. What procedural adjustment should the internal auditing function make to align with this organizational change?

options.A: Increase the frequency of routine audits to check for implementation errors.
options.B: Develop a work program specifically targeting the post-upgrade period.
options.C: Delay all ongoing audits until the upgrade is completed successfully.
options.D: Conduct surveys among accounting staff on their readiness for the upgrade.

question: During the planning phase of an engagement, an engagement supervisor identifies potential risks relating to the organization’s compliance with new regulatory requirements. What should be the immediate next step the supervisor takes to incorporate these risks into the engagement work program?

options.A: Schedule additional meetings with the regulatory compliance team to confirm the risks.
options.B: Increase the overall engagement budget to absorb the potential risks.
options.C: Develop specific procedures in the work program to address these identified risks.
options.D: Assign more senior auditors to the engagement to manage observed risks.

question: The best description of the primary purpose of the engagement work program is to

options.A: List all potential risks within an audit.
options.B: Serve as a principal record of audit work and conclusions.
options.C: Outline the criteria for evaluating engagement objectives.
options.D: Document procedures to be performed during an engagement.

question: While reviewing an engagement work program, an auditor notes that key controls were not tested. What should the auditor do to ensure all objectives are met?

options.A: Proceed with other tasks and report the findings as incomplete.
options.B: Notify the engagement supervisor and request a review of the program.
options.C: Adjust the work program independently to include key controls.
options.D: Document the oversight and move on.

question: An internal auditor discovers that the engagement team’s work program lacks clear evaluation criteria. What action should the auditor take?

options.A: Create the evaluation criteria and proceed.
options.B: Consult with the CAE to revise the work program and incorporate criteria.
options.C: Ignore the lack of criteria because the work program has been previously approved.
options.D: Perform the tasks without criteria and conclude intuitively.

question: An internal audit supervisor is reviewing the engagement work program to ensure it is adequate. What is the best way to evaluate its adequacy?

options.A: Comparing the work program to previous audits without considering engagement specifics.
options.B: Assessing whether the activities proposed align with engagement objectives and identified risks.
options.C: Reducing the number of procedures to streamline audit efficiency.
options.D: Focusing only on regulatory compliance without assessing operational risks.

question: An auditor is assessing the engagement work program for completeness before execution. What criterion should be used to determine its adequacy?

options.A: Using only high-level objectives without specifying detailed activity.
options.B: Verifying that the program includes as many activities as possible, regardless of relevance.
options.C: Limiting the scope of activities in order to minimize audit time.
options.D: Ensuring the program includes clear activities, timelines, and responsibilities.

question: An audit manager is evaluating whether an engagement work program is sufficient to achieve the audit objectives. What factor is most important in determining its adequacy?

options.A: Prioritizing control design without specific testing to assess control effectiveness.
options.B: Confirming that the work program follows the same format as previous audits.
options.C: The opportunity for multiple audit team member involvement.
options.D: Ensuring that the activities planned effectively address all identified risks.

question: Which of the following documents should the internal auditor examine to determine whether only authorized purchases are being accepted by the receiving department?

options.A: A bill of lading.
options.B: A copy of the purchase order.
options.C: An invoice.
options.D: Policies and procedures for the receiving function.

question: An organization uses electronic data interchange and online systems rather than paper-based documents for purchase orders, receiving reports, and invoices. Which of the following audit procedures would an auditor use to determine if invoices are paid only for goods received and at approved prices?

options.A: Select a statistical sample of major vendors and trace the amounts paid to specific invoices.
options.B: Use generalized audit software to select a sample of payments and match purchase orders, invoices, and receiving reports stored on the computer using a common reference.
options.C: Select a monetary-unit sample of accounts payable and confirm the amounts directly with the vendors.
options.D: Use generalized audit software to identify all receipts for a particular day and trace the receiving reports to checks issued.

question: An auditor selected items for test counts while observing physical inventory. The auditor then traced the test counts to the inventory listing. Tracing test counts most likely obtained evidence concerning the relevant assertion about

options.A: Rights and obligations.
options.B: Completeness.
options.C: Existence.
options.D: Accuracy, valuation, and allocation.

question: Which of the following procedures provides the most relevant information to determine the adequacy of the allowance for doubtful accounts receivable?

options.A: Confirm the receivables.
options.B: Analyze the following month’s payments on the accounts receivable balances outstanding.
options.C: Test the controls over the write-off of accounts receivable to ensure that management approves all write-offs.
options.D: Analyze the allowance through an aging of receivables and an analysis of current economic data.

question: During a post-completion engagement related to a warehouse expansion, the internal auditor noted several invoices for redecorating services from a local merchant that were account-coded and signed for payment only by the cost engineer. The internal auditor should

options.A: Compare the cost and description of the services with the account code used in the construction project and with related estimates in the construction-project budget.
options.B: Consult with the cost engineer for assurance that these purchases were authorized for this construction project.
options.C: Obtain a facsimile of the cost engineer’s signature from the accounts payable group and compare it with the signature on the invoices.
options.D: Recommend reclassifying the expenditure to the appropriate account code for redecorating services.

question: The internal auditor wishes to test the assertion that all claims paid by a medical insurer contain proper authorization and documentation, including but not limited to the validity of the claim from an approved physician and an indication that the claim complies with the claimant’s policy. The most appropriate engagement procedure is to select a sample of

options.A: All policyholders and examine all claims for the sampled items during the year to determine whether the claims were handled properly.
options.B: Claims filed and trace to documentary information about authorization and other supporting documentation.
options.C: Claims denied and determine that all claims denied were appropriate. The claims denied file is much smaller and the internal auditor can obtain greater coverage with the sample size.
options.D: Paid claims from the claims (cash) disbursement file and vouch to documentary information about authorization and other supporting documentation.

question: An internal auditor wishes to determine whether salaried employees in the division being audited are taking more paid vacation time than they have earned. Which of the following audit procedures will be most effective?

options.A: Observing which employees were absent because of vacations and tracing those absences through the payroll records to subtractions from accumulated vacation time.
options.B: Comparing total vacation time taken by selected employees in the most recent 12 months per payroll records to the time taken by the same employees in the preceding 12 months.
options.C: Sending confirmations to selected employees, asking them to verify the accuracy of the number of days of vacation used during the year and the number of remaining unused days as obtained from the payroll records.
options.D: Comparing the accrued vacation pay liability as computed for the organization’s most recent balance sheet with the corresponding amount for 1 year earlier and investigating any significant change.

question: An internal auditor has set an engagement objective of ascertaining the reasonableness of the increases in rental revenue resulting from operating costs passed on to the lessee by the landlord. The internal auditor has already inspected the lease contract to determine that such costs are allowed. Which of the following engagement procedures will best meet this objective?

options.A: Inspection of documents.
options.B: Observation.
options.C: Inquiry.
options.D: Analytical review.

question: An auditor’s purpose in reviewing the renewal of a note payable shortly after the balance sheet date most likely is to obtain evidence concerning relevant assertions about

options.A: Existence.
options.B: Classification.
options.C: Completeness.
options.D: Accuracy, valuation, and allocation.

question: Which of the following engagement objectives will be accomplished by tracing a sample of accounts receivable debit entries to customer invoices and related shipping documents?

options.A: Sales are properly recorded.
options.B: Sales are billed at the correct prices.
options.C: Accounts receivable represent valid sales.
options.D: Customer credit is approved.

question: Vouching entails verifying recorded amounts by examining the underlying documents from the _____ documents to the _____ documents.

options.A: Final; original.
options.B: Final; previous.
options.C: Original; final.
options.D: Original; subsequent.

question: An internal auditor has set an engagement objective of determining whether mail room staff is fully used. Which of the following engagement techniques will best meet this objective?

options.A: Inspection of documents.
options.B: Observation.
options.C: Inquiry.
options.D: Analytical review.

question: Which of the following represents the most reliable information that a receivable actually exists?

options.A: A positive confirmation.
options.B: A sales invoice.
options.C: A receiving report.
options.D: A bill of lading.

question: Of the following, the information collected by the internal auditor during an engagement is best described as

options.A: The records of preliminary planning and surveys, the engagement work program, and the results of field work.
options.B: The information documented by the internal auditor and obtained through observing conditions, interviewing people, and examining records.
options.C: An intermediate fact, or group of facts, from which the internal auditor can infer the fairness of an assertion being reviewed.
options.D: Detailed documentation for systems that do not achieve desired objectives, actions that were taken improperly, and actions that should have been taken but were not.

question: Observation is considered a reliable engagement procedure, but one that is limited in usefulness. However, it is used in a number of different engagement situations. Which of the following statements is true regarding observation as an engagement technique?

options.A: It is the most effective engagement methodology to use in filling out internal control questionnaires.
options.B: It is the most persuasive methodology to learn how transactions are really processed during the period under review.
options.C: It is rarely sufficient to satisfy any assertion other than existence.
options.D: It is the most persuasive technique for determining if fraud has occurred.

question: An internal auditor is observing cash sales to determine whether customers are given written receipts. The objective of this test is to ensure that

options.A: Cash received equals the total of the receipts.
options.B: Customers are charged authorized prices.
options.C: Cash balances are correct.
options.D: All cash sales are recorded.

question: An internal audit function is planning an assurance engagement in the transportation department of a large engineering firm. The firm owns and operates a fleet of cars and trucks of various sizes. One engagement objective is to evaluate the department’s vehicle maintenance procedures. Which of the following procedures is most appropriate for this engagement objective?

options.A: Interview the controller to gather information about maintenance procedures and their cost.
options.B: Compare procedure costs with internal cost standards set by management.
options.C: Analyze accident insurance claims.
options.D: Interview service technicians to gather information about maintenance procedures.

question: Confirmations are a highly regarded form of information. Confirmation is most effective in addressing the existence assertion for the

options.A: Addition of a milling machine to a machine shop.
options.B: Sale of merchandise during regular course of business.
options.C: Inventory held on consignment.
options.D: Granting of a patent for a special process developed by the organization.

question: Which of the following documents provides the most persuasive information concerning the existence and valuation of a receivable?

options.A: A credit approval document supported by the customer’s audited financial statements.
options.B: A copy of a sales invoice to the customer in the department’s records.
options.C: A positive confirmation received directly from the customer.
options.D: A customer’s purchase order in the department’s records related to the credit sale.

question: An internal auditor traces copies of sales invoices to shipping documents to determine that

options.A: Customer shipments were billed.
options.B: Sales that are billed were also shipped.
options.C: Shipments to customers were also recorded as receivables.
options.D: The subsidiary accounts receivable ledger was updated.

question: To determine whether refunds granted to customers were properly approved, an internal auditor should vouch accounts receivable entries to

options.A: Sales invoices.
options.B: Remittance advices.
options.C: Shipping documents.
options.D: Credit memos.

question: Shipping documents should be traced to and compared with sales records or invoices to

options.A: Determine whether payments are properly applied to customer accounts.
options.B: Assure that shipments are billed to customers.
options.C: Determine whether unit prices billed are in accordance with sales contracts.
options.D: Ascertain whether all sales are supported by shipping documents.

question: An internal auditor has set an engagement objective of identifying the existence of personality conflicts that are detrimental to productivity. Which of the following engagement techniques will best meet this objective?

options.A: Inspection of documents.
options.B: Observation.
options.C: Inquiry.
options.D: Analytical review.

question: An internal auditor has set an engagement objective of ascertaining compliance with a city ordinance forbidding city purchasing from vendors affiliated with elected city officials. Which of the following engagement techniques will best meet this objective?

options.A: Inspection of documents.
options.B: Observation.
options.C: Inquiry.
options.D: Analytical review.

question: An organization manufacturing special-order products is experiencing excessive rates of rejection of finished products. An engagement procedure to identify the source of the problem is

options.A: Evaluating communications from the sales department to the production department.
options.B: Evaluating communications from the production department to the sales department.
options.C: Analyzing customer demand for the product.
options.D: Testing whether supply of the product is sufficient to meet customer demand.

question: An internal auditor observes that controls over the perpetual inventory system are weak. An appropriate engagement response is to

options.A: Increase the testing of the inventory controls.
options.B: Perform turnover ratio tests.
options.C: Recommend that a physical inventory count be scheduled.
options.D: Apply gross profit analyses by product lines and compare the results with prior years’ information for reasonableness.

question: Which technique is most appropriate for testing the quality of the preliminary survey of payment vouchers described in an internal control questionnaire?

options.A: Analysis.
options.B: Evaluation.
options.C: Verification.
options.D: Observation.

question: An internal auditor of an organization in the process of acquiring another organization has been requested to verify that cash for the organization being acquired is properly stated. The engagement technique that will yield the most persuasive piece of information is

options.A: Examining the organization’s escheatment account.
options.B: Interviewing the organization’s chief financial officer and cash manager.
options.C: Obtaining standard bank confirmations.
options.D: Comparing current cash in the bank with previous accounting periods through analytical computations.

question: To identify the amount of obsolete inventory that may exist in an organization, an internal auditor probably collects information using several procedures. Which of the following is the least helpful in identifying the amount of obsolete inventory?

options.A: Confirmation.
options.B: Scanning.
options.C: Recomputation.
options.D: Analytical review.

question: One engagement procedure for an engagement to evaluate facilities and equipment is to test the accuracy of recorded depreciation. Which of the following is the best source of information that the equipment in question is in service?

options.A: A review of depreciation policies and procedures.
options.B: A comparison of depreciation schedules with a listing of insurance appraisals for the same equipment.
options.C: A comparison of depreciation schedules with the maintenance and repair logs for the same equipment.
options.D: A review of inventory documentation for the equipment.

question: Management believes that some specific sales commissions for the year were too large. The accuracy of the recorded commission expense for specific salespersons is best determined by

options.A: Computation of selected sales commissions.
options.B: Calculating commission ratios.
options.C: Use of analytical procedures.
options.D: Tests of overall reasonableness.

question: Which of the following engagement procedures will provide the least relevant information for determining that payroll payments were made to bona fide employees?

options.A: Reconcile time cards in use to employees on the job.
options.B: Examine canceled checks for proper endorsement and compare to personnel records.
options.C: Test for segregation of the authorization for payment from the hire/fire authorization.
options.D: Test the payroll account bank reconciliation by tracing outstanding checks to the payroll register.

question: Which of the tests provides the least significant information when testing for suspected fraudulent sales?

options.A: Tracing a sample of authorized inventory slips from inventory through billing to the sales journal.
options.B: Performing analytical tests of sales by comparing sales and gross margins over time.
options.C: Performing analysis of write-offs and sales returns and comparing the amounts over the past several years.
options.D: Confirming sales transactions with customers and investigating nonresponses.

question: Which of the following is the most appropriate engagement procedure to test the processing of interbank transfers?

options.A: Analyze a sample of interbank transfers throughout the period including period-end reconciliations.
options.B: Obtain cutoff bank statements for each bank account and reconcile them to accounting records.
options.C: Send bank confirmation requests to each bank in which accounts are maintained and reconcile the completed forms to accounting records.
options.D: Trace all bank deposits recorded in accounting records near the end of the fiscal period to supporting documentation and to bank statements.

question: To ascertain that all credit sales are recorded in accounts receivable, an internal auditor should

options.A: Confirm selected accounts receivable balances by direct correspondence with customers.
options.B: Trace from a sample of subsidiary ledger entries to related sales invoices and to related shipping documents.
options.C: Trace from a sample of customer purchase orders to related shipping documents.
options.D: Trace from a sample of shipping documents to related sales invoices and subsidiary ledger.

question: An organization has outsourced many services, including waste collection, cafeteria, and custodial services previously performed internally. Management requests an evaluation of contract compliance and the overall performance of the organizations performing the outsourced activities. Which of the following engagement procedures is the least effective in accomplishing the engagement objectives?

options.A: Comparison of current costs with the costs of performing the same services before they were outsourced.
options.B: Comparison of charges with the terms of the outsourcing contract.
options.C: A survey of users’ satisfaction with the services performed by the outsourcer.
options.D: Comparison of identified activities for each outsourcer with “best practices” of other outsourcers.

question: To control daily operating costs, an organization decreased the number of times a messenger service was used each day. Despite those measures, the monthly bill continued to increase. What procedure should the internal auditor use to detect whether improper services were being billed?

options.A: Reconcile a sample of messenger invoices to pickup receipts.
options.B: Test the mathematical accuracy of a sample of messenger invoices.
options.C: Scan ledger accounts and messenger invoices.
options.D: Observe daily use of the messenger service.

question: Which of the following procedures is most appropriate for testing whether cost overruns on a construction project were caused by the contractor improperly accounting for costs related to contract change orders?

options.A: Compare costs billed to date to original cost estimates.
options.B: Verify that the change orders were properly approved by management.
options.C: Verify that the contractor has not charged costs for change orders that have already been billed or for original contract work that was canceled.
options.D: Compare change order costs with other change order costs for similar projects in the past.

question: A charitable organization solicits donations by phone and email. The generation of calling and mailing lists, the level of success of each solicitation, and the tracking of amounts pledged are performed electronically. Which of the following is the least satisfactory procedure for obtaining assurance about the completeness of recorded amounts pledged?

options.A: Review of recordings of phone calls and archives of email messages.
options.B: Analytical procedures comparing previous years’ per-call amounts pledged with this year’s.
options.C: Random monitoring of phone calls and email traffic.
options.D: Mailed confirmations of amounts pledged.

question: Which of the following statements about audit evidence is true?

options.A: A copy of a source document has less evidential value than the original.
options.B: Physical observation of accounts payable is the most convincing form of evidence to support the assertion of completeness.
options.C: A purchase order marked “paid” is persuasive evidence for the receipt of goods.
options.D: To be representative of a population, a sample must contain at least 10% of the items in the population.

question: An entity is beginning its budget cycle. Approval of the capital budget by the board of directors is the first step in the process. Until final approval, only the CEO and division vice presidents have access to it. During the multiple iterations of the capital budget, hard copies are printed and distributed to authorized persons or their administrative assistants. Which of the following is the most effective procedure by an internal auditor to gain assurance that IT personnel are not distributing the capital budget reports to unauthorized employees?

options.A: Interviewing computer operations personnel and reviewing logs of abnormal program terminations.
options.B: Interviewing IT personnel responsible for programming the budgetary applications.
options.C: Reviewing the log signed by those receiving the reports.
options.D: Interviewing all authorized personnel or their administrative assistants to determine whether they received the reports.

question: Which audit procedure would be most effective to detect whether a particular employee may have been involved in the submission of payments to false vendors?

options.A: Send confirmations to a sample of vendors to determine whether they received proper payments.
options.B: Implement an integrated test facility and monitor transactions throughout the year to identify unusual items.
options.C: Implement the snapshot approach to tag unusually large increases related to the employee.
options.D: Use generalized audit software to sort payments by employee, then by common addresses and names.

question: A production manager for a moderate-sized manufacturer began ordering excessive raw materials and had them delivered to a wholesale business that the manager was running on the side. The manager falsified receiving documents and approved the invoices for payment. Which of the following procedures is most likely to detect this fraud?

options.A: Take a sample of cash disbursements; compare purchase orders, receiving reports, invoices, and check copies.
options.B: Take a sample of cash disbursements; confirm the amount purchased, purchase price, and date of shipment with the vendors.
options.C: Observe the receiving dock and count materials received; compare the counts with receiving reports completed by receiving personnel.
options.D: Perform analytical tests, comparing production, materials purchased, and raw materials inventory levels; investigate differences.

question: The manager of a production line has the authority to order and receive replacement parts for all machinery that requires periodic maintenance. The internal auditor received an anonymous tip that the manager ordered substantially more parts than were necessary from a family member in the parts supply business. The unneeded parts were never delivered. Instead, the manager processed receiving documents and charged the parts to machinery maintenance accounts. The payments for the undelivered parts were sent to the supplier, and the money was divided between the manager and the family member. Which of the following tests would best assist the auditor in deciding whether to investigate this anonymous tip further?

options.A: Comparison of the current quarter’s maintenance expense with prior-period activity.
options.B: Physical inventory testing of replacement parts for existence and valuation.
options.C: Analysis of repair parts charged to maintenance to review the reasonableness of the number of items replaced.
options.D: Review of a test sample of parts invoices for proper authorization and receipt.

question: The internal auditor reviewed documentation showing that a customer had recently returned three expensive products to the regional service center for warranty replacement. The documentation also showed that the warranty clerk had rejected the claim and sent it to the customer’s local distributor. The claim was rejected because the serial numbers listed in the warranty claim were not found in the computer’s sales history file. Subsequently, the distributor supplied three different serial numbers, all of which were validated by the computer system, and the clerk completed the warranty claim for replacements. What is the best course of action for the internal auditor under the circumstances?

options.A: Determine if the original serial numbers provided by the customer can be traced to other records, such as production and inventory records.
options.B: Notify the appropriate authorities within the organization that there are sufficient indicators that a fraud has been committed.
options.C: Verify with the appropriate supervisor that the warranty clerk had followed relevant procedures in the processing and disposition of this claim.
options.D: Summarize this item along with other valid transactions in the internal auditor’s test of warranty transactions.

question: While reviewing a division’s accounts, an internal auditor becomes concerned that the division’s management may have shipped poor quality merchandise to boost sales and profitability and thereby increase the manager’s bonus. For this reason, the internal auditor suspects that returned goods are being shipped to other customers as new products without full correction of their defects. Which of the following engagement procedures is ineffective in determining whether such shipments took place?

options.A: Examine credit memos issued after year end for goods shipped before year end.
options.B: Physically observe the shipping and receiving area for information of returned goods.
options.C: Interview customer service representatives regarding unusual amounts of customer complaints.
options.D: Require the division to take a complete physical inventory at year end, and observe the taking of the inventory.

question: Contributions to a nonprofit organization have been constant for the past 3 years. The audit committee has become concerned that the president may have embarked on a scheme in which some of the contributions from many sustaining members have been redirected to other organizations. The audit committee suspects that the scheme may involve taking major contributions and depositing them in alternative accounts or soliciting contributions to be made in the name of another organization. Which of the following procedures should be most effective in detecting the existence of such a fraud?

options.A: Use generalized audit software to take a sample of pledged receipts not yet collected and confirm the amounts due with the donors.
options.B: Take a sample that includes all large donors for the past 3 years and a statistical sample of others and request a confirmation of total contributions made to the organization or to affiliated organizations.
options.C: Take a discovery sample of cash receipts and confirm the amounts of the receipts with the donors. Investigate any differences.
options.D: Use analytical review procedures to compare contributions generated with those of other comparable institutions over the same period of time. If the amount is significantly less, take a detailed sample of cash receipts and trace to the bank statements.

question: The internal auditor suspects a disbursements fraud in which an unknown employee(s) is submitting and approving invoices for payment. Before discussing the potential fraud with management, the internal auditor decides to gather additional information. Which of the following procedures is most helpful in providing the additional information?

options.A: Use software to develop a list of vendors with post office box numbers or other unusual features. Select a sample of those items and trace to supporting documents such as receiving reports.
options.B: Select a sample of payments made during the year and investigate each one for approval.
options.C: Select a sample of receiving reports representative of the period under investigation and trace to approved payment. Note any items not properly processed.
options.D: Take a sample of invoices received during the past month, examine to determine whether properly authorized for payment, and trace to underlying documents.

question: During an engagement, the internal auditor found a scheme in which the warehouse director and the purchasing agent for a retail organization diverted a significant amount of goods to their own warehouse, then sold the goods to third parties. The fraud was not noted earlier because the warehouse director forwarded receiving reports (after updating the perpetual inventory records) to the accounts payable department for processing. Which of the following procedures most likely led to the discovery of the missing materials and the fraud?

options.A: Take a random sample of receiving reports and trace to the recording in the perpetual inventory record. Note differences and investigate by type of product.
options.B: Take a random sample of purchase orders and trace them to receiving documents and to the records in the accounts payable department.
options.C: Take an annual physical inventory, reconciling amounts with the perpetual inventory, noting the pattern of differences and investigating.
options.D: Take a random sample of sales invoices and trace to the perpetual records to see if inventory was on hand. Investigate any differences.

question: The internal auditor finds a situation in which one person has the ability to collect receivables, make deposits, issue credit memos, and record receipt of payments. The internal auditor suspects the individual may be stealing from cash receipts. Which of the following engagement procedures is most effective in discovering fraud in this scenario?

options.A: Send positive confirmations to a random selection of customers.
options.B: Send negative confirmations to all outstanding accounts receivable customers.
options.C: Perform a detailed review of debits to customer discounts, sales returns, or other debit accounts, excluding cash posted to the cash receipts journal.
options.D: Take a sample of bank deposits and trace the detail in each bank deposit back to the entry in the cash receipts journal.

question: Management has requested that the internal auditor investigate the possibility that a purchasing agent is receiving kickbacks. Which of the following procedures is least effective in addressing management’s concern?

options.A: Confirm all contract terms with vendors.
options.B: Analyze, by purchasing agent, all increases in cost of procured goods from specific vendors.
options.C: Take a statistical sample of goods purchased and compare purchase prices for goods with those of other sources of similar goods, such as other organizations or catalogs.
options.D: Observe any changes in the lifestyles or individual consumption habits of the purchasing agents involved.

question: When testing the year-end balance for trade accounts payable, the use of a software package to identify unauthorized vendors in a vendor database is most valuable in developing tests to determine

options.A: Existence of valid recorded liabilities.
options.B: Accuracy of the receiving cutoff used.
options.C: Ownership of the recorded payables.
options.D: Valuation of recorded transactions.

question: An accounting clerk developed a scheme to enter fraudulent invoices into the computer system for nonexistent vendors. All the payments were sent to the same address. The internal auditor suspects a possible fraud. The internal auditor should test all of the vendor information rather than a sample of the vendor transactions because

options.A: Although nonsampling error is reduced, sampling error is larger when computers are used to draw the sample.
options.B: The engagement procedures used to compare vendor information require the reading of all records.
options.C: The Standards prohibit the use of sampling if fraud is expected.
options.D: The only effective approach requires performing procedures “through the computer.”

question: An internal auditor becomes concerned that fraud, in the form of payments to bogus entities, may exist. Buyers, who are responsible for all purchases for specific product lines, are able to approve expenditures up to $50,000 without any other approval. Which of the following procedures would be most effective in addressing the internal auditor’s concerns?

options.A: Use generalized audit software to list all purchases over $50,000 to determine whether the expenditures were properly approved.
options.B: Develop a “snapshot” technique to trace all transactions by suspected buyers.
options.C: Use generalized audit software to take a random sample of all expenditures under $50,000 to determine whether the expenditures were properly approved.
options.D: Use generalized audit software to list all major vendors by product line; select a sample of paid invoices to new vendors and examine information indicating that services or goods were received.

question: Fact Pattern: Bank management suspects that a bank loan officer frequently made loans to fictitious entities, disbursed loan proceeds to personally established accounts, and then let the loans go into default. Some pertinent facts about the loan officer include Not taking vacations; An expensive personal car; Gasoline and repair bills submitted for a car assigned by the bank that are higher than the organization’s average; and Occasionally showing impatience with questions from internal auditors. The extent of loans made to fictitious borrowers by the loan officer could best be determined by

options.A: Reviewing a representative sample of the loan officer’s transactions for compliance with bank policies and procedures.
options.B: Reviewing a representative sample of loan files for properly completed documents, such as loan agreements, credit approvals, and approval of secured collateral.
options.C: Comparing current loan approval balances with those of prior years.
options.D: Requesting positive confirmations for all outstanding loans made by the loan officer.

question: Fact Pattern: Bank management suspects that a bank loan officer frequently made loans to fictitious entities, disbursed loan proceeds to personally established accounts, and then let the loans go into default. Some pertinent facts about the loan officer include Not taking vacations; An expensive personal car; Gasoline and repair bills submitted for a car assigned by the bank that are higher than the organization’s average; and Occasionally showing impatience with questions from internal auditors. All of the following procedures help determine the extent of the loans made to fictitious borrowers by the loan officer except

options.A: Analyses of the number of loans made by each loan officer.
options.B: Analysis of total monetary volume of loans by loan officer.
options.C: External audits of loan files.
options.D: Reconciliation of total loans outstanding to the general ledger balance.

question: Purchases from two new vendors increased dramatically after a new buyer was hired. The buyer was obtaining kickbacks from the two vendors based on sales volume. A possible means of detection is

options.A: Periodically surveying vendors regarding potential buyer conflict of interest or ethics violations.
options.B: The receipt of an invoice to put new vendors on the master file.
options.C: The use of purchase orders for all purchases.
options.D: The use of change analysis and trend analysis of buyer or vendor activity.

question: One remote unit’s petty cash custodian, because of the small staff, also had responsibility for the imprest fund checking account reconciliation. The cashier concealed a diversion of funds by altering the beginning balance on the monthly reconciliations sent to the group office. A possible engagement procedure to detect this fraud is to

options.A: Compare monthly balances and use change and trend analysis.
options.B: Require additional monitoring by headquarters whenever improper segregation of duties exists at remote units.
options.C: Determine whether any employees have high personal debt.
options.D: Determine whether any employees are leading expensive lifestyles.

question: An internal auditor is more likely to detect duplicate vendor payments in a high exposure environment with certain internal control weaknesses by using which of the following procedures?

options.A: Trend analysis.
options.B: Monetary validity.
options.C: Proportional analysis.
options.D: Substantive testing.

question: A subsidiary president terminated a controller and hired a replacement without the required organizational approvals. Sales, cash flow, and profit statistics were then manipulated by the new controller and president via accelerated depreciation and sale of capital assets to obtain larger performance bonuses for the controller and the subsidiary president. An approach that might detect this fraudulent activity is

options.A: Analysis of overall management control for segregation of duties.
options.B: Required exit interviews for all terminated employees.
options.C: Periodic changes of outside public accountants.
options.D: Regular analytical review of operating divisions.

question: An employee of an insurer processed a fraudulent policy loan application for an amount less than the established level requiring supervisory review. The employee then obtained the check and cashed it by forging the endorsement. To prevent the loan’s appearance on a subsequent policyholder statement, the loan amount was transferred to a “suspense” account. Which of the following should expose this situation at the earliest date?

options.A: A computer report identifying unusual entries to the suspense account.
options.B: The use of prenumbered checks that are periodically accounted for.
options.C: An annual engagement performed by the internal audit function.
options.D: Regular reconciliation of the “suspense” account performed by an independent employee.

question: An internal auditor is investigating the performance of a division with an unusually large increase in sales, gross margin, and profit. If the internal auditor continued to suspect fraudulent recording of transactions to increase reported profits, which of the following procedures would be least effective?

options.A: Take a physical inventory.
options.B: Develop a schedule of inventory by month and investigate unusual fluctuations by reference to the perpetual inventory records.
options.C: Prepare a schedule of sales fluctuations and gross margin by month. Investigate unusually high months of sales and gross margin by examining support for sales.
options.D: Perform year-end sales and purchase cut-off tests.

question: An internal auditor is investigating the performance of a division with an unusually large increase in sales, gross margin, and profit. Assume that the analysis shows unusually high sales and gross margin during the months of November and December and the internal auditor wishes to investigate further. Which of the following engagement procedures will be most effective in analyzing whether fraudulent sales may have been recorded?

options.A: Take a sample of shipping documents and compare them with the related sales invoices, noting that all items were properly billed.
options.B: Confirm accounts receivable with large customers.
options.C: Perform an analytical review comparing sales and gross margin with the previous 10 months and the first month of the following year.
options.D: Use regression analysis techniques for the first 10 months to estimate the sales and cost of goods sold for the last 2 months.

question: Fact Pattern: An internal auditor is performing an operational engagement at a division and observes that an unusually large quantity of goods is on hand in the shipping and materials rework areas. The items are labeled as re-ship items. Upon inquiry the internal auditor is told that these are goods that have been returned by customers and have either been repaired and shipped back to the original customer or repaired and shipped out as new products because they are fully warranted. The internal auditor has not yet performed any detailed engagement work. Based on the information given, the most appropriate action for the internal auditor to take is to

options.A: Report the items to divisional management and ask for management’s explanation before determining whether to include the observations in an engagement communication.
options.B: Take a sample of the items on hand and compare the sample items with the underlying documents, such as receiving reports and sales orders, to determine how the goods were handled.
options.C: Report the observations but do not perform any additional work without the approval of the chief audit executive because such work is clearly a scope expansion.
options.D: Take an inventory of the goods on hand so the monetary amount can be included in the engagement communications along with the explanation of the problem.

question: An auditor for a major retail company suspects that inventory fraud is occurring at three stores that have high cost of goods sold. Which of the following audit activities would provide the most persuasive evidence that fraud is occurring?

options.A: Use an integrated test facility (ITF) to compare individual sales transactions with test transactions submitted through the ITF. Investigate all differences.
options.B: Interview the three individual store managers to determine if their explanations about the observed differences are the same, and then compare their explanations to that of the section manager.
options.C: Schedule a surprise inventory audit to include a physical inventory. Investigate areas of inventory shrinkage.
options.D: Select a sample of individual store prices and compare them with the sales entered on the cash register for the same items.

context: The auditor of a construction company that builds foundations for bridges and large buildings performed a review of the expense accounts for equipment (augers) used to drill holes in rocks to set the foundation for the buildings. During the review, the auditor noted that the expenses related to some of the auger accounts had increased dramatically during the year. The auditor inquired of the construction manager who offered the explanation that the augers last 2 to 3 years and are expensed when purchased. Thus, the auditor should see a decrease in the expense accounts for these augers in the next year but would expect an increase in the expenses of other augers. The auditor also found out that the construction manager is responsible for the inventorying and receiving of the augers and is a part owner of a company that supplies augers to the company. The supplier was approved by the president of the company to improve the quality of equipment.
question: Which of the following procedures is the least appropriate engagement procedure to address these analytical observations?

options.A: Note the explanation in the workpapers for investigation during the next engagement and perform no further work at this time.
options.B: Develop a comparative analysis of auger expense over the past few years to determine if the relationship held in previous years.
options.C: Take a sample of debits to the auger expense account and trace to independent shipping documents and to invoices for the augers.
options.D: Arrange to take an inventory of augers to determine if the augers purchased this year were on hand and would be available for use in the next 2 years.

question: An internal auditor is considering whether the amount of cash is accurately recorded on the financial statements. All of the following are appropriate engagement procedures for the objective except

options.A: Examining bank reconciliations and confirming bank balances.
options.B: Comparing cash receipt lists with the receipts journal and bank deposit slips.
options.C: Verifying cutoff of receipts and disbursements.
options.D: Adding totals of reconciliations and comparing with cash account balances.

question: Which of the following engagement procedures provides the best information about the collectibility of notes receivable?

options.A: Confirmation of note receivable balances with the debtors.
options.B: Examination of notes for appropriate debtors’ signatures.
options.C: Reconciliation of the detail of notes receivable and the provision for uncollectible amounts to the general ledger control.
options.D: Examination of cash receipts records to determine promptness of interest and principal payments.

question: An internal auditor for a large service organization is performing an engagement to review the organization’s cash balance. The internal auditor is considering the most appropriate engagement procedure to use to ensure that the amount of cash is accurately recorded on the financial statements. The most appropriate engagement procedures for the objective are

options.A: Review collection procedures and perform an analytical review of accounts receivable; confirm balances of accounts receivable; and verify the existence of appropriate procedures and facilities.
options.B: Compare cash receipt lists to the receipts journal and bank deposit slips; review the segregation of duties, and observe and test cash receipts.
options.C: Review the organizational structure and functional responsibilities; verify the existence of, and describe protection procedures for, unused checks, including security measures.
options.D: Examine bank reconciliations, confirm bank balances, and verify cutoff of receipts and disbursements; foot totals of reconciliations and compare to cash account balances.

question: Subsequent to the acquisition of a new subsidiary, the internal audit function is validating reports from subsidiary management. Which of the following areas will the internal auditor corroborate with the external organizational counsel?

options.A: Credit lines.
options.B: Collateral arrangements.
options.C: Contingency estimates.
options.D: Accounts receivable balances.

question: As part of a preliminary survey of the purchasing function, an auditor read the department’s policies and procedures manual. The auditor concluded that the manual described the processing steps well and contained an appropriate internal control design. The next engagement objective was to determine the operating effectiveness of internal controls. Which procedure would be most appropriate in meeting this objective?

options.A: Prepare a flowchart.
options.B: Prepare a system narrative.
options.C: Perform a test of controls.
options.D: Perform a substantive test.

question: An audit found that the cost of some material installed on capital projects had been transferred to the inventory account because the capital budget had been exceeded. Which of the following would be an appropriate technique for the internal audit function to use to monitor this situation?

options.A: Identify variances between amounts capitalized each month and the capital budget.
options.B: Analyze a sample of capital transactions each quarter to detect instances in which installed material was transferred to inventory.
options.C: Review all journal entries that transferred costs from capital projects accounts to inventory accounts.
options.D: Compare inventory receipts with debits to the inventory account and investigate discrepancies.

question: In an engagement to evaluate an automated inventory control system, which approach provides the best information that purchase orders are authorized?

options.A: Tracing purchase orders to the computer listing.
options.B: Comparing receiving reports with purchase order details.
options.C: Testing to ensure that only authorized persons are able to change parameters in the program that generates purchase orders.
options.D: Reviewing system documentation to determine proper functioning of the program.

question: A population of entries in the fixed assets file from the current period and the next period is an appropriate population to sample if the audit objective is to determine whether

options.A: Expenditures for fixed assets have been improperly expensed.
options.B: Capital expenditures were properly authorized.
options.C: Noncapital repair expenditures have been properly expensed.
options.D: Expenditures for fixed assets have been recorded in the proper period.

question: To determine the competence of the personnel in the purchasing department, an internal auditor most likely should perform

options.A: Analytical procedures.
options.B: Inquiries of the staff.
options.C: Tests of controls.
options.D: Substantive procedures.

question: Which of the following engagement procedures, performed by the internal auditor, is most likely to detect this fraud?

options.A: Tracing selected canceled checks to the cash payments journal and to the related vendors’ invoices.
options.B: Performing a trend analysis of printing supplies expenses for a 2-year period.
options.C: Tracing prices and quantities on selected vendors’ invoices to the related purchase orders.
options.D: Recomputing the clerical accuracy of selected vendors’ invoices, including discounts and sales taxes.

question: An engagement objective is to determine if a company’s accounts payable contain all outstanding liabilities. All of the following audit procedures are relevant for this objective except

options.A: Examine supporting documentation of subsequent (after-period) cash disbursements and verify period of liability.
options.B: Send confirmations, including zero-balance accounts, to vendors with whom the company normally does business.
options.C: Select a sample of accounts payable from the accounts payable listing and verify the supporting receiving reports, purchase orders, and invoices.
options.D: Trace receiving reports issued before the period end to the related vendor invoices and accounts payable listing.

question: Determining that proper amounts of depreciation are expensed provides assurance about management’s assertions of valuation and allocation and

options.A: Classification and understandability.
options.B: Completeness.
options.C: Rights and obligations.
options.D: Occurrence.

question: If the objective of an auditor’s test of details is to detect the overstatement of sales, the auditor should vouch transactions from the

options.A: Sales journal to the shipping documents.
options.B: Shipping documents to the cash receipts journal.
options.C: Cash receipts journal to the customer’s purchase orders.
options.D: Customer’s purchase orders to the sales journal.

question: When performing procedures to test assertions about purchases, an auditor vouches a sample of entries in the voucher register to the supporting documents. Which relevant assertion would this procedure most likely support?

options.A: Completeness.
options.B: Occurrence.
options.C: Valuation and allocation.
options.D: Classification.

question: An auditor who wishes to test for the occurrence of equity transactions should complete which of the following procedures?

options.A: Compare prior-period amounts to current amounts.
options.B: Vouch entries to supporting documents.
options.C: Inquire with shareholders about the date that a stock purchase occurred.
options.D: Inspect stock certificates held in treasury.

question: Which of the following might be detected by an auditor’s review of the sales cutoff?

options.A: Excessive goods returned for credit.
options.B: Unrecorded sales discounts.
options.C: Lapping of year-end accounts receivable.
options.D: Inflated sales for the year.

question: A cutoff test of sales complements the verification of

options.A: Sales returns.
options.B: Cash.
options.C: Accounts receivable.
options.D: Sales allowances.

question: In confirming with an outside agent, such as a financial institution, that the agent is holding investment securities in the organization’s name, an auditor most likely gathers evidence in support of relevant financial statement assertions about existence or occurrence and

options.A: Valuation and allocation.
options.B: Rights and obligations.
options.C: Completeness.
options.D: Classification and understandability.

question: In establishing the existence and ownership of an investment held by a corporation in the form of publicly traded stock, an auditor should inspect the securities or

options.A: Obtain written representations from management confirming that the securities are properly classified as trading securities.
options.B: Inspect the audited financial statements of the investee company.
options.C: Confirm the number of shares owned that are held by an independent custodian.
options.D: Determine that the investment is carried at the lower of cost or market.

question: An auditor inspects an organization’s investment records to determine that any transfers between categories of investments have been properly recorded. The primary purpose of this procedure is to obtain evidence concerning relevant financial statement assertions about

options.A: Rights and obligations, and existence.
options.B: Valuation and allocation, and rights and obligations.
options.C: Existence or occurrence, and classification and understandability.
options.D: Classification and understandability, and valuation and allocation.

question: Tests designed to detect purchases made before the end of the year that have been recorded in the subsequent year most likely would provide assurance about the relevant assertion regarding

options.A: Valuation and allocation.
options.B: Existence.
options.C: Cutoff.
options.D: Classification and understandability.

question: Which of the following statements is an internal auditor most likely to add to the negative form of confirmation of accounts receivable to encourage timely consideration by the recipient?

options.A: “This is not a request for payment; remittances should not be sent to our internal auditors in the enclosed envelope.”
options.B: “Report any differences on the enclosed statement directly to our internal auditors; no reply is necessary if this amount agrees with your records.”
options.C: “If you do not report any differences within 15 days, it will be assumed that this statement is correct.”
options.D: “The following invoices have been selected for confirmation and represent amounts that are overdue.”

question: In the confirmation of accounts receivable, the auditor would most likely

options.A: Request confirmation of a sample of the inactive accounts.
options.B: Seek to obtain positive confirmations for at least 50% of the total dollar amount of the receivables.
options.C: Require confirmation of all receivables from agencies of the federal government.
options.D: Require that confirmation requests be sent within 1 month of the fiscal year end.

question: Negative confirmation of accounts receivable is less effective than positive confirmation of accounts receivable because

options.A: A majority of recipients usually lack the willingness to respond objectively.
options.B: Some recipients may report incorrect balances that require extensive follow-up.
options.C: The internal auditor cannot infer that all nonrespondents have verified their account information.
options.D: Negative confirmations do not produce evidence that is statistically quantifiable.

question: When counting cash on hand, the internal auditor must exercise control over all cash and other negotiable assets to prevent

options.A: Theft.
options.B: Irregular endorsement.
options.C: Substitution.
options.D: Deposits in transit.

question: Bank teller supervisors might manipulate accounts using their privileged computer access codes. They could withdraw money for their own use and move money among accounts when depositors complain to the bank about errors. The audit procedure most likely to detect this is

options.A: Reviewing transactions on privileged access codes.
options.B: Reviewing transactions for employees’ accounts.
options.C: Verifying proof records for teller access codes.
options.D: Testing the accuracy of account posting programs.

question: An internal auditor is concerned about the possibility of fraud if

options.A: Cash receipts, net of the amounts used to pay petty cash-type expenditures, are deposited in the bank daily.
options.B: The monthly bank statement reconciliation is performed by the same employee who maintains the perpetual inventory records.
options.C: The accounts receivable subsidiary ledger and accounts payable subsidiary ledger are maintained by the same person.
options.D: One person, acting alone, has sole access to the petty cash fund (except for a provision for occasional surprise counts by a supervisor or auditor).

question: Which of the following procedures concerning accounts receivable is an internal auditor most likely to perform to obtain evidence in support of the effectiveness of controls?

options.A: Observing an entity’s employee prepare the schedule of past due accounts receivable.
options.B: Sending confirmation requests to an entity’s principal customers to verify the existence of accounts receivable.
options.C: Inspecting an entity’s analysis of accounts receivable for unusual balances.
options.D: Comparing an entity’s uncollectible accounts expense with actual uncollectible accounts receivable.

question: Before performing substantive analytical procedures at an interim date prior to the balance sheet date, an internal auditor should

options.A: Obtain audit evidence about the operating effectiveness of controls.
options.B: Determine that the accounts selected for interim testing are not material to the financial statements taken as a whole.
options.C: Consider whether the amounts of the year-end balances selected for interim testing are reasonably predictable.
options.D: Obtain written representations from management that all financial records and related data will be made available.

question: An audit assistant found a purchase order for a regular supplier in the amount of $5,500. The purchase order was dated after receipt of the goods. The purchasing agent had forgotten to issue the purchase order. Also, a disbursement of $450 for materials did not have a receiving report. The assistant wanted to select additional purchase orders for investigation but was unconcerned about the lack of a receiving report. The audit director should

options.A: Agree with the assistant because the amount of the purchase order exception was considerably larger than the receiving report exception.
options.B: Agree with the assistant because the cash disbursement clerk had been assured by the receiving clerk that the failure to fill out a report did not happen very often.
options.C: Disagree with the assistant because the two problems have an equal risk of loss associated with them.
options.D: Disagree with the assistant because the lack of a receiving report has a greater risk of loss associated with it.

question: An internal auditor performs a test to determine whether all merchandise for which the organization was billed was received. The population for this test consists of all

options.A: Merchandise received.
options.B: Vendors’ invoices.
options.C: Canceled checks.
options.D: Receiving reports.

question: In a payables application, checks are authorized and paid based on matching purchase orders, receiving reports, and vendor invoices. Partial payments are common. An appropriate audit procedure for verifying that a purchase order has not been paid twice is to sort the

options.A: Receiving report file by purchase order, compute total amounts received by purchase order, compare total amounts received with purchase order amounts, and investigate any discrepancies between the total amounts received and purchase order amounts.
options.B: Vendor invoice file by purchase order, compute total amounts invoiced by purchase order, compare total amounts invoiced with purchase order amounts, and investigate any discrepancies between the total amounts invoiced and purchase order amounts.
options.C: Receiving report file by vendor invoice amounts and investigate any discrepancies between the total amounts received and vendor invoice amounts.
options.D: Check register file by purchase order, compute total amounts paid by purchase order, compare total amounts paid with purchase order amounts, and investigate any discrepancies between the total amounts paid and purchase order amounts.

question: In assessing risks of material misstatement for purchases, an internal auditor vouches a sample of entries in the voucher register to the supporting documents. Which assertion would this test of controls most likely support?

options.A: Completeness.
options.B: Occurrence.
options.C: Accuracy.
options.D: Classification.

question: Your objective is to determine that nonrecurring purchases, initiated by various user organizations, have been properly authorized. If all purchases are made through the purchasing department, to which of the following documents should you vouch purchases?

options.A: Purchase requisitions.
options.B: Purchase orders.
options.C: Invoices.
options.D: Receiving reports.

question: Which is the best audit procedure to obtain evidence to support the legal ownership of real property?

options.A: Examination of corporate minutes and board resolutions with regard to approvals to acquire real property.
options.B: Examination of closing documents, deeds, and ownership documents registered and on file at the county courthouse.
options.C: Discussion with corporate legal counsel concerning the acquisition of a specific piece of property.
options.D: Confirmation with the title company that handled the escrow account and disbursement of proceeds for the closing of the property.

question: An internal auditor analyzes repairs and maintenance accounts primarily to obtain evidence in support of the classification assertion that all

options.A: Noncapitalizable expenditures for repairs and maintenance have been recorded in the proper period.
options.B: Expenditures for property and equipment have been recorded in the proper period.
options.C: Noncapitalizable expenditures for repairs and maintenance have been properly charged to expense.
options.D: Expenditures for property and equipment have not been charged to expense.

question: In violation of a company policy, Lowell Company erroneously capitalized the cost of painting its warehouse. The internal auditor examining Lowell’s financial statements would most likely detect this error when

options.A: Discussing capitalization policies with Lowell’s controller.
options.B: Examining maintenance expense accounts.
options.C: Observing, during the physical inventory observation, that the warehouse had been painted.
options.D: Examining the construction work orders supporting items capitalized during the year.

question: If the objective of a test of details is to detect overstatements of sales, an internal auditor should compare transactions in the

options.A: Cash receipts journal with the sales journal.
options.B: Sales journal with the cash receipts journal.
options.C: Source documents with the accounting records.
options.D: Accounting records with the source documents.

question: An internal auditor reconciles the total of the accounts receivable subsidiary ledger to the general ledger control account, as of October 31. By this procedure, the auditor would be most likely to learn of which of the following?

options.A: An October invoice was improperly computed.
options.B: An October check from a customer was posted in error to the account of another customer with a similar name.
options.C: An opening balance in a subsidiary ledger account was improperly carried forward from the previous accounting period.
options.D: An account balance is past due and should be written off.

question: Identification of an appropriate population to sample is dependent upon audit objectives. A population of entries in an asset repairs expense file is an appropriate population if the audit objective is to determine whether

options.A: Expenditures for fixed assets have been improperly expensed.
options.B: Noncapital repair expenditures have been properly charged to expense.
options.C: Noncapital repair expenditures have been recorded in the proper period.
options.D: Expenditures for fixed assets have been recorded in the proper period.

question: During a preliminary survey for an engagement, an auditor uses walkthroughs to understand the business processes. Which assertion does this technique most directly support?

options.A: Existence.
options.B: Completeness.
options.C: Valuation.
options.D: Rights and obligations.

question: While planning an engagement to audit the procurement processes of a large manufacturing company, the internal auditor finds potential risks related to unapproved vendor transactions. What should the auditor’s focus be to address these risks effectively?

options.A: Increase financial statement testing to uncover discrepancies.
options.B: Perform detailed testing of vendor contracts and transaction approvals.
options.C: Interview procurement staff to understand the procurement cycle.
options.D: Create an inventory reconciliation to verify materials discrepancies.

question: An internal audit team is investigating a series of high procurement costs in a branch of a manufacturing company. What is the most appropriate approach to identify potential inefficiencies or irregularities?

options.A: Interview procurement staff about purchasing practices.
options.B: Compare current procurement costs with historical data and industry benchmarks.
options.C: Review all recent purchase orders and invoices.
options.D: Conduct a physical inspection of procured goods to verify need.

question: When engaging with a highly creative and decentralized marketing department, what is the most appropriate audit procedure to understand the department’s controls over its activities?

options.A: Review financial statements for the marketing department’s expenses.
options.B: Perform a walkthrough of the marketing department’s daily operations.
options.C: Interview the head of marketing on control effectiveness.
options.D: Conduct a survey of all marketing staff about control practices.

question: According to The IIA Standards, what is the most persuasive form of evidence for internal auditors?

options.A: Oral testimony.
options.B: Information originating from a third party.
options.C: Auditor’s physical examination.
options.D: Inspection of original documents.

question: An internal auditor is reviewing an organization’s compliance with contractual obligations in its lease agreements. Which audit procedure is most effective in verifying that the lease terms are accurately reported in the organization’s financial statements?

options.A: Conducting interviews with the legal department about lease interpretations.
options.B: Verifying leases through confirmation with landlords.
options.C: Tracing lease details from agreements to financial records.
options.D: Observing lease negotiations at organization meetings.

question: An internal auditor is performing an audit that involves both financial and operational aspects in a dynamic retail company. What should be emphasized to gather persuasive evidence for such a multifaceted audit?

options.A: Focus on financial statement verification procedures.
options.B: Incorporate both analytical procedures and detailed substantive testing.
options.C: Concentrate on interviews and personnel feedback to acquire qualitative information.
options.D: Delegate the operational aspects of the audit to an external team.

question: A company has implemented a new approval workflow for expense reimbursements. What procedure should an auditor use to assess the control design?

options.A: Conducting a random survey on employee adherence to policies.
options.B: Interviewing employees to determine their satisfaction with the workflow.
options.C: Comparing approval workflows to those used by competitors.
options.D: Reviewing process documentation to verify segregation of duties.

question: An auditor is assessing the design of an organization’s password management policy. What is the best method to evaluate its effectiveness?

options.A: Reviewing password change frequency to determine compliance with security policies.
options.B: Comparing the policy requirements to established industry cybersecurity standards.
options.C: Conducting employee interviews to assess awareness of password management guidelines.
options.D: Analyzing system logs to identify trends in password resets and potential weaknesses.

question: A retail company has implemented an automated inventory reconciliation system. What is the most effective procedure to assess whether the control design is adequate?

options.A: Surveying employees to measure their confidence in the system and its impact on reconciliation accuracy.
options.B: Conducting structured interviews with inventory staff to evaluate usability and process alignment.
options.C: Comparing inventory reports before and after automation to assess the impact on accuracy and efficiency.
options.D: Reviewing system configurations to verify reconciliation thresholds and approval settings.

question: An auditor is evaluating the control design for vendor payment authorization in an accounts payable system. What procedure would be most effective?

options.A: Reviewing the timeliness of past vendor payments.
options.B: Asking vendors for feedback on the payment process.
options.C: Examining workflow approvals to verify appropriate authorization levels.
options.D: Observing employees processing payments to identify efficiency gaps.

question: A financial institution has implemented a new transaction monitoring system to detect fraudulent activity. What procedure should be used to evaluate the control design?

options.A: Surveying customers about their trust in the institution’s fraud prevention efforts.
options.B: Monitoring daily transaction logs for unusual activity.
options.C: Reviewing attendance of employees at training sessions on fraud detection.
options.D: Reviewing system rules to determine if they align with known fraud risk indicators.

question: An internal auditor is testing the efficiency of an automated payroll processing system. What is the most effective procedure?

options.A: Checking if payroll errors have been reported in the past year.
options.B: Interviewing employees to assess their satisfaction with the payroll system.
options.C: Comparing payroll policies to industry best practices.
options.D: Measuring the time taken for payroll processing before and after automation.

question: A company has implemented a workflow automation system for purchase order approvals. What procedure should be used to test the efficiency of this control?

options.A: Comparing approval workflows across different departments.
options.B: Surveying employees about their experience with the automated system.
options.C: Reviewing a sample of purchase orders to check for policy compliance.
options.D: Analyzing the average approval time before and after automation.

question: A healthcare provider introduced electronic medical record (EMR) automation. What is the best way to test the efficiency of this control?

options.A: Evaluating patient record retrieval times before and after implementation.
options.B: Conducting patient satisfaction surveys about digital records.
options.C: Checking compliance with health data protection laws.
options.D: Comparing system usage among different departments.
