question: A financial institution adopted automated risk assessment for loan approvals. What is the most effective way to test the efficiency of this control?

options.A: Comparing automated approval rates to manual ones.
options.B: Reviewing policies on risk assessment criteria.
options.C: Interviewing underwriters about their experience with the automated system.
options.D: Analyzing loan processing times before and after automation.

question: An internal auditor is conducting an engagement focused on IT system access controls. What testing methodology would be most effective?

options.A: Surveying employees to assess their satisfaction with IT security policies.
options.B: Performing a sample-based user access review to verify adherence to access control policies.
options.C: Comparing access control settings to those used by other organizations.
options.D: Reviewing system documentation without testing actual user access.

question: An auditor is assessing the accuracy of financial transactions in an organization’s accounting system. Which testing methodology would be most appropriate?

options.A: Reviewing the general ledger to verify recorded balances without testing underlying transactions for accuracy.
options.B: Conducting structured interviews with accounting staff to assess their understanding of financial accuracy controls.
options.C: Distributing a company-wide survey to gather employee perceptions on financial statement transparency and reporting.
options.D: Performing substantive testing by selecting a sample of transactions and tracing them to supporting documentation.

question: In determining the effectiveness of an entity’s policies and procedures relating to the occurrence assertion for payroll transactions, an auditor most likely would inquire about and

options.A: Observe the segregation of duties concerning human resources responsibilities and payroll disbursement.
options.B: Inspect evidence of accounting for prenumbered payroll checks.
options.C: Recompute the payroll deductions for employee fringe benefits.
options.D: Verify the preparation of the monthly payroll account bank reconciliation.

question: The internal auditor is concerned about whether all the debits to the computer security expense account are appropriate expenditures. The most appropriate engagement procedure is to

options.A: Take an attribute sample of computing invoices and determine whether all invoices are properly classified.
options.B: Perform an analytical review comparing the amount of expenditures incurred this year with the amounts incurred on a trend line for the past 5 years.
options.C: Take an attribute sample of employee wage expenses incurred by the outsourcing organization and trace to the proper account classification.
options.D: Take a sample of all debits to the account and investigate by examining source documents to determine the nature and authority of the expenditure.

question: For review of an accounting department’s bank reconciliation unit, which of the following is an appropriate engagement work program step for the review of canceled checks for authorized signatures?

options.A: Comparing the check date with the first cancellation date.
options.B: Determining that all checks are to be signed by individuals authorized by the board.
options.C: Examining a representative sample of signed checks and determining that the signatures are authorized in the organizational signature book.
options.D: Completing the tests of controls over check signatures in 4 hours.

question: A bank internal auditor wanted to verify the accuracy of the general ledger balance of a depository account. One engagement procedure used in this process was to mail positive confirmations to statistically sampled depositors. However, the number of replies received was not adequate to form a valid conclusion about the account’s accuracy. What action should the internal auditor take to accomplish this objective?

options.A: Assume that the nonreplies represent tacit agreements by the depositor, document the results, and perform no further work on this engagement procedure.
options.B: Expand the original confirmation sample to include additional depositors.
options.C: Verify accuracy of the depositors’ addresses. Remail confirmation requests a second time with a notation indicating that it is a second request.
options.D: Mail negative confirmation requests to all non-replies and document results of testing. If necessary, telephone depositors to inquire about any disagreement with balances confirmed.

question: To test whether debits to accounts receivable represent valid transactions, the internal auditor should trace entries from the

options.A: Sales journal to the accounts receivable ledger.
options.B: Accounts receivable ledger to the cash receipts journal.
options.C: Accounts receivable ledger to sales documentation.
options.D: Cash receipts documentation to the accounts receivable ledger.

question: One of the audit objectives for a manufacturing company is to verify that all rework is reviewed by the production engineer. Which of the following audit procedures would provide the best evidence for meeting this objective?

options.A: Trace a sample of entries in the rework log to remedial action taken.
options.B: Trace a sample of rework orders to entries in the rework log.
options.C: Trace a sample of entries in the review log to rework orders.
options.D: Trace a sample of rework orders to entries in the review log.

question: An internal auditor traces individual time tickets to the payroll cost distribution and also traces totals from the payroll cost distribution to the various work-in-process accounts. If no exceptions are found, this procedure constitutes information indicating that

options.A: The work-in-process accounts have not been padded by the inclusion of unsupported payroll costs.
options.B: Individual time tickets have been properly authorized.
options.C: Payroll costs have been accurately distributed to work-in-process accounts.
options.D: Employees have been paid only for time actually worked.

question: A production manager ordered excessive raw materials for delivery to a separate company owned by the manager. The manager falsified receiving documents and approved the invoices for payment. Which of the following audit procedures would most likely detect this fraud?

options.A: Select a sample of cash disbursements and compare purchase orders, receiving reports, invoices, and check copies.
options.B: Select a sample of cash disbursements and confirm the amount purchased, purchase price, and date of shipment with the vendors.
options.C: Observe the receiving dock and count materials received; compare the counts to receiving reports completed by receiving personnel.
options.D: Perform analytical tests, comparing production, materials purchased, and raw materials inventory levels; investigate differences.

question: An internal auditor has set an engagement objective of determining whether the planned rate of return on investment in international operations has been achieved. Which of the following engagement procedures will best meet this objective?

options.A: Inspection of documents.
options.B: Observation.
options.C: Inquiry.
options.D: Analytical review.

question: Which of the substantive field work procedures presented below provides the best information about completeness of recorded revenues?

options.A: Reconciling the sales journal to the general ledger control account.
options.B: Vouching charges made to the accounts receivable subsidiary ledger to supporting shipping records.
options.C: Vouching shipping records to the customer order file.
options.D: Reconciling shipping records to recorded sales.

question: A large manufacturer has a transportation division that supplies gasoline for the organization’s vehicles. Gasoline is dispensed by an attendant who records the amount issued on a serially prenumbered gasoline disbursement form, which is then given to the accounting department for proper recording. When the quantity of gasoline falls to a certain level, the service station attendant prepares a purchase requisition and sends it to the purchasing department where a purchase order is prepared and recorded in a gasoline purchases journal. Which of the following engagement procedures best determines whether gasoline disbursements are fully recorded?

options.A: Compare the gasoline purchase requisitions with the gasoline disbursement records.
options.B: Select a number of gasoline purchases from the gasoline purchases journal and compare them with their corresponding purchase orders. Ascertain that the purchases are serially prenumbered, are matched with purchase requisitions, and are authorized by someone independent of employees of the service station.
options.C: Perform analytical procedures comparing this period’s gasoline consumption with prior periods.
options.D: Match the quantity of gasoline disbursed according to disbursement forms with an independent reading of quantity disbursed at the pump.

question: Cash receipts should be deposited on the day of receipt or the following business day. Select the most appropriate engagement procedure to determine that cash is promptly deposited.

options.A: Review cash register tapes prepared for each sale.
options.B: Review the functions of cash handling and maintaining accounting records for proper segregation of duties.
options.C: Compare the daily cash receipts totals with the bank deposits.
options.D: Review the functions of cash receiving and disbursing for proper segregation of duties.

question: During an engagement to evaluate travel expenses, the accounting supervisor tells the internal auditor that each expense report is reviewed and approved before costs are reimbursed to the traveler. Which of the following is the best course of action for the internal auditor to take?

options.A: Request the supervisor to put the statement in writing.
options.B: Review a sample of expense reports for proper approval.
options.C: Conserve engagement resources by accepting the statement and redirect work into another area.
options.D: Corroborate this information with the controller.

question: A transportation department maintains its vehicle inventory and maintenance records in a database. Which of the following audit procedures is most appropriate for evaluating the accuracy of the database information?

options.A: Verify a sample of the records extracted from the database with supporting documentation.
options.B: Submit batches of test transactions through the current system and verify with expected results.
options.C: Simulate normal processing by using test programs.
options.D: Use program tracing to show how, and in what sequence, program instructions are processed in the system.

question: Which of the following procedures would provide the best evidence of the effectiveness of a credit-granting function?

options.A: Observe the process.
options.B: Review the trend in receivables write-offs.
options.C: Ask the credit manager about the effectiveness of the function.
options.D: Check for evidence of credit approval on a sample of customer orders.

question: Fact Pattern: An organization has grown rapidly and has just automated its human resource system. The organization has developed a large database that tracks employees, employee benefits, payroll deductions, job classifications, ethnic code, age, insurance, medical protection, and other similar information. Management has asked the internal audit function to review the new system. To test whether data currently within the automated system are correct, the internal auditor should

options.A: Use test data and determine whether all the data entered are captured correctly in the updated database.
options.B: Take a sample of data to be entered for a few days and trace the data to the updated database to determine the correctness of the updates.
options.C: Obtain a printout of all employees with invalid job descriptions and investigate the causes of the problems.
options.D: Select a sample of employees from the database and verify the data fields.

question: To determine whether credit controls are inconsistently applied, preventing valid sales to creditworthy customers, the internal auditor should

options.A: Confirm current accounts receivable.
options.B: Trace postings on the accounts receivable ledger.
options.C: Analyze collection rates and credit histories.
options.D: Compare credit histories for those receiving credit and for those denied credit.

question: A manufacturer uses a materials requirements planning (MRP) system to track inventory, orders, and raw material requirements. A preliminary audit assessment indicates that the organization’s inventory is understated. Using audit software, what conditions should the auditor search for in the MRP database to support this hypothesis?

options.A: Item costs set to zero and negative quantities on hand.
options.B: Order costs exceeding industry standards.
options.C: Inventory lead times exceeding the delivery schedule.
options.D: Order quantity exceeding requirements.

question: Management has requested an audit of promotional expenses. The sales department has been giving away items in conjunction with new product sales to stimulate demand. The promotion is successful, but management believes the cost may be too high. The least useful procedure to determine the effectiveness of the promotion is

options.A: An analysis of marginal revenue and marginal cost for the promotion period and the prior period.
options.B: A review of the sales department’s reasons for believing that the promotion has been successful.
options.C: A comparison of product sales during the promotion period with sales during a similar nonpromotion period.
options.D: A comparison of the unit cost of the products sold before and during the promotion period.

question: Inventory levels for a packing facility are controlled by just-in-time (JIT) methods. If the auditor’s objective is to evaluate ordering and stocking standards, which of the following procedures are most relevant?

options.A: Calculating the cost of quality.
options.B: Using audit software to calculate the shipping crates used and quantities shipped and comparing actual stocking levels with industry averages.
options.C: Reviewing sales records for unsatisfied customers.
options.D: Comparing the actual products sold with management forecasts.

question: During an engagement relating to purchasing, the internal auditor finds that the largest blanket purchase order is for tires, which are expensed as vehicle maintenance items. The fleet manager requisitions tires against the blanket order for the company’s 400-vehicle service fleet based on a visual inspection of the cars and trucks in the parking lot each week. Sometimes the fleet manager picks up the tires but always signs the receiving report for payment. Vehicle service data are entered into a maintenance database by the mechanic after the tires are installed. What is the best course of action for the internal auditor in these circumstances?

options.A: Determine whether the number of tires purchased can be reconciled to maintenance records.
options.B: Count the number of tires on hand and trace them to the related receiving reports.
options.C: Select a judgmental sample of requisitions and verify that each one is signed by the fleet manager.
options.D: Compare the number of tires purchased under the blanket purchase order with the number of tires purchased in the prior year for reasonableness.

question: An investment portfolio manager has the authority to use financial derivatives to hedge transactions but is not supposed to take speculative positions. However, the manager launches a scheme that includes (1) taking a position larger than required by the hedge, (2) putting the speculative gains in a suspense account, and (3) transferring the funds to a nonexistent broker and from there to a personal account. Which of the following engagement procedures is least effective in detecting this fraud?

options.A: Examine individual trades to determine whether the trades violate the authorization limit for the manager.
options.B: Sample individual trades and determine the exact matching of a hedge. Schedule and investigate all differences.
options.C: Sample all debits to the suspense account and examine their disposition.
options.D: Sample fund transfers to brokers and determine if the brokers are on the organization’s authorized list for transactions.

question: Two merging retail enterprises agree to share data on store operations. The data reveal that three stores in Organization A are characterized by: Significantly lower gross margins, Higher-than-average sales volume, and Higher levels of employee bonuses. Assume the internal auditor for the merged enterprise concludes that inventory fraud is the most reasonable explanation of the observed data. Which of the following engagement procedures will provide the most persuasive information that fraud is taking place?

options.A: Use an integrated test facility (ITF) to compare individual sales transactions with test transactions submitted through the ITF. Investigate all differences.
options.B: Interview the three individual store managers to determine if their explanations about the observed differences are the same. Compare their explanations with those of the section manager.
options.C: Schedule a surprise physical inventory. Investigate areas of inventory shrinkage.
options.D: Take a sample of individual store prices and compare them with the sales entered on the cash register for the same items.

question: Fact Pattern: Bank management suspects that a bank loan officer frequently made loans to fictitious entities, disbursed loan proceeds to personally established accounts, and then let the loans go into default. Some pertinent facts about the loan officer include Not taking vacations; An expensive personal car; Gasoline and repair bills submitted for a car assigned by the bank that are higher than the organization’s average; and Occasionally showing impatience with questions from internal auditors. The most appropriate trend analysis to indicate this potential fraud is

options.A: Loan default rates by loan officer.
options.B: Accumulation of unpaid vacation days.
options.C: Automobile operating expenses by loan officer.
options.D: Total monetary volume of loans by loan officer.

question: Which of the following procedures would be most helpful in providing additional evidence when an auditor suspects that an unidentified employee is submitting and approving invoices for payment?

options.A: Use generalized audit software to identify invoices from vendors with post office box numbers or other unusual features. Select a sample of those invoices and trace to supporting documents such as receiving reports.
options.B: Select a sample of payments made during the year and investigate each one for approval.
options.C: Select a sample of receiving reports representative of the period under investigation and trace to approved payment. Note any items not properly processed.
options.D: Select a sample of invoices paid during the past month and trace them to appropriate vendor accounts.

question: An engagement objective is to determine whether an organization’s liabilities for accounts payable are complete. Which audit procedure is least relevant to this objective?

options.A: Examine documents supporting cash payments after the end of the period and verify the period of liability.
options.B: Send confirmations of zero-balance accounts to vendors with which the organization normally does business.
options.C: Select a sample of accounts payable transactions from the accounts payable listing dated near the end of the current period and the beginning of the following period.
options.D: Trace receiving reports issued before the period end to the related vendor invoices and accounts payable listing.

question: An engagement to review payroll is least likely to include

options.A: Tests of computations for gross and net wages.
options.B: Comparison of payroll costs to budget.
options.C: Tracing a sample of employee names to employment records in the personnel department.
options.D: Observing the physical distribution of paychecks.

question: An organization makes a practice of investing excess short-term cash in marketable equity securities. A reliable test of the valuation of those securities is a

options.A: Comparison of cost data with current market quotations.
options.B: Confirmation of securities held by the broker.
options.C: Recalculation of investment carrying amount using the equity method.
options.D: Calculation of premium or discount amortization.

question: An internal auditor is testing the assertion that all claims paid by an insurer are properly authorized and documented. Testing addresses, among other things, whether claims are valid and consistent with claimants’ policies. The most appropriate engagement procedure is to select a sample of

options.A: Claimants and verify a sample of documents gathered prior to policy acceptance.
options.B: Claims filed and vouch to supporting documents to test authorization.
options.C: Claims denied and determine whether all denials were appropriate.
options.D: Claims paid and vouch to supporting documents.

question: Shipments are made from the warehouse based on customer purchase orders. The matched shipping documents and purchase orders are then forwarded to the billing department for sales invoice preparation. The shipping documents are neither accounted for nor prenumbered. Which of the following substantive tests should be extended as a result of this control weakness?

options.A: Select sales invoices from the sales register and examine the related shipping documents.
options.B: Select bills of lading from the warehouse and trace the shipments to the related sales invoices.
options.C: Foot the sales register and trace the total to the general ledger.
options.D: Trace quantities and prices on the sales invoice to the customer purchase order and test extensions and footings.

question: An auditor observes the mailing of monthly statements to customers and reviews evidence of follow-up on errors reported by the customers. This test of controls most likely is performed to support management’s financial statement assertion(s) of

options.A: Classification andUnderstandability Yes Existence Yes
options.B: Classification andUnderstandability Yes Existence No
options.C: Classification andUnderstandability No Existence Yes
options.D: Classification andUnderstandability No Existence No

question: During an audit of a company’s equity accounts, the auditor determines whether restrictions have been imposed on retained earnings resulting from loans, agreements, or state law. This audit procedure most likely is intended to verify relevant assertion about

options.A: Existence or occurrence.
options.B: Completeness.
options.C: Valuation and allocation.
options.D: Classification and understandability.

question: An auditor selects a sample of recorded cash receipts and vouches them to accounts receivable and customer orders. This procedure is relevant to which assertion?

options.A: Completeness.
options.B: Existence.
options.C: Cutoff.
options.D: Occurrence.

question: An organization sells 15 to 20 units of product annually. A large portion of the annual sales occur in the last month of the fiscal year. Annual sales have not materially changed over the past 5 years. Which of the following approaches would be most effective concerning the timing of audit procedures for revenue?

options.A: The auditor should perform analytical procedures at an interim date and discuss any changes in the level of sales with senior management.
options.B: The auditor should inspect transactions occurring in the last month of the fiscal year and review the related sale contracts to determine that revenue was posted in the proper period.
options.C: The auditor should perform tests of controls at an interim date to obtain audit evidence about the operational effectiveness of internal controls over sales.
options.D: The auditor should review period-end compensation to determine if bonuses were paid to meet earnings goals.

question: Treetop Corporation acquired a building and arranged mortgage financing during the year. Verification of the related mortgage acquisition costs most likely include an examination of the related

options.A: Closing statement and the deed.
options.B: Canceled checks and recorded interest expense.
options.C: Closing statement, canceled checks, and interest expense.
options.D: A written confirmation from an accountant.

question: An auditor traces the daily remittance list to the last validated deposit ticket for the period. Which of the following assertions is being tested?

options.A: Completeness.
options.B: Valuation and allocation.
options.C: Accuracy.
options.D: Existence.

question: Which of the following is a substantive procedure that an auditor most likely would perform to verify the existence and valuation assertions about recorded accounts payable?

options.A: Investigating the open purchase order file to ascertain that prenumbered purchase orders are used and accounted for.
options.B: Receiving the organization’s mail, unopened, for a reasonable period of time after year end to search for unrecorded vendor’s invoices.
options.C: Vouching selected entries in the accounts payable subsidiary ledger to purchase orders and receiving reports.
options.D: Confirming accounts payable balances with known suppliers who have zero balances.

question: In confirming accounts receivable, an internal auditor decided to confirm customers’ account balances rather than individual invoices. Which of the following most likely will be included with the organization confirmation letter?

options.A: An auditor-prepared letter explaining that a nonresponse may cause an inference that the account balance is correct.
options.B: An organization-prepared letter reminding the customer that a nonresponse will cause a second request to be sent.
options.C: An auditor-prepared letter requesting the customer to supply missing and incorrect information directly to the organization.
options.D: An organization-prepared statement of account showing the details of the customer’s account balance.

question: During the process of confirming receivables as of December 31, Year 1, a positive confirmation was returned indicating the “balance owed as of December 31 was paid on January 9, Year 2.” The internal auditor would most likely

options.A: Determine whether any changes in the account occurred between January 1 and January 9, Year 2.
options.B: Determine whether a customary trade discount was taken by the customer.
options.C: Reconfirm the zero balance as of January 10, Year 2.
options.D: Verify that the amount was received.

question: An internal auditor’s observation of physical inventories at the main plant at year end provides direct evidence to support which of the following objectives?

options.A: Accuracy of the priced-out inventory.
options.B: Evaluation of lower of cost or market test.
options.C: Identification of obsolete or damaged merchandise to evaluate allowance (reserve) for obsolescence.
options.D: Determination of goods on consignment at another location.

question: During the preliminary survey phase of an audit of the organization’s production cycle, management stated that the sale of scrap was well controlled. Evidence to verify that assertion can best be gained by

options.A: Comparing current revenue from scrap sales with that of prior periods.
options.B: Interviewing persons responsible for collecting and storing the scrap.
options.C: Comparing the quantities of scrap expected from the production process with the quantities sold.
options.D: Comparing the results of a physical inventory of scrap on hand with perpetual inventory records.

question: What should a CAE consider as a primary attribute when selecting engagement procedures for a specific audit?

options.A: Cost-effectiveness of procedures.
options.B: Currency of auditing standards.
options.C: Relevance to engagement objectives.
options.D: Availability of necessary technology.

question: During a financial audit, the internal auditor notices discrepancies in transaction records that could relate to the completeness assertion. What action should the auditor take next?

options.A: Perform additional sampling of transactions.
options.B: Discuss discrepancies with operational management and seek explanations.
options.C: Trace transactions from source documents to financial records.
options.D: Observe subsequent transaction handling procedures.

question: During an internal audit in a financial organization, the auditor suspects an internal control failure related to cash handling, resulting in unrecorded cash transactions. Which audit procedure should the auditor perform to confirm this suspicion?

options.A: Conduct a surprise count of cash on hand.
options.B: Interview the cashier about cash handling processes.
options.C: Review past internal audit reports for inconsistencies.
options.D: Validate the existence of physical safes and security systems.

question: During a financial audit, the team suspects fraud due to irregularities in accounts receivable. What procedures should they prioritize to verify their suspicions?

options.A: Examine physical inventory records.
options.B: Perform a tracing procedure from invoices to shipping documents.
options.C: Perform a cutoff test of the accounts.
options.D: Send confirmations to verify account balances with customers.

question: A company has introduced an automated reconciliation process for financial reporting. What procedure should be used to test whether the control is operating effectively?

options.A: Reviewing non-reconciliation volumes.
options.B: Selecting a sample of reconciliations and verifying accuracy against supporting records.
options.C: Checking whether the reconciliation process aligns with competitor practices.
options.D: Reviewing the training materials provided to employees on reconciliation policies.

question: A company requires manager approval for all expense reimbursements over a certain threshold. What procedure should be performed to assess the effectiveness of this control?

options.A: Interviewing managers to determine their process for reviewing and approving reimbursements.
options.B: Reviewing a sample of expense reports to confirm approvals were obtained as required.
options.C: Conducting an employee survey to assess compliance with the reimbursement approval policy.
options.D: Analyzing approval trends over time to evaluate whether the policy is consistently enforced.

question: An organization has introduced role-based access controls (RBAC) for system security. What is the best procedure to assess the efficiency of these controls?

options.A: Conducting a survey to determine employee opinions on security restrictions.
options.B: Reviewing system logs to evaluate the speed of access approval processes.
options.C: Comparing access control policies with those of industry competitors.
options.D: Interviewing IT staff about their experience managing access requests.

question: An auditor is assessing the accuracy of financial transactions in an organization’s accounting system. Which testing methodology would be most appropriate?

options.A: Interviewing accounting staff about their perception of financial accuracy.
options.B: Performing substantive testing by selecting a sample of transactions and tracing them to supporting documentation.
options.C: Conducting a company-wide survey on financial statement transparency.
options.D: Reviewing the general ledger without verifying individual transactions.

question: According to IIA guidance, which of the following data analytics methods would yield the most relevant information for an internal auditor trying to identify payments made to unapproved suppliers?

options.A: Match accounts receivable and bank statements.
options.B: Match accounts payable and the vendor master file.
options.C: Match the vendor master file and employees’ data files.
options.D: Match purchase order files and accounts payable.

question: During an audit engagement, you are examining the organization’s statement of comprehensive income. You notice that some other comprehensive income (OCI) items are classified as revenues. What should be your course of action if you want to assess the potential effects on financial reporting integrity?

options.A: Confirm that classification changes align with recent changes in accounting standards.
options.B: Recalculate the financial ratios to assess the effects on financial performance.
options.C: Discuss with management whether it is aware of these classification errors.
options.D: Assess whether these errors are material and recommend restatements if necessary.

question: An organization wants to identify all risks that could affect strategy and business objectives. Which of the following risk-related concepts does this situation represent?

options.A: Inherent risk.
options.B: Risk and control matrix.
options.C: Risk capacity.
options.D: Risk appetite.

question: While auditing a technology firm’s customer relationship management (CRM) system, the internal auditor finds that data access is not strictly controlled. What is a potential risk associated with this finding?

options.A: Increased system downtime.
options.B: Uncontrolled financial reporting adjustments.
options.C: Unauthorized access to sensitive customer information.
options.D: Improved cross-department collaboration.

question: Which of the following observations by an auditor is most likely to indicate the existence of control weaknesses over safeguarding of assets?

options.A: A service department’s location is not well suited to allow adequate service to other units.
options.B: A significant number of identified control weaknesses related to inventory control have been corrected.
options.C: Managers do not have access to reports that profile overall performance in relation to other benchmarked organizations.
options.D: Employees hired for sensitive positions are not subjected to background checks.

context:
A member of the audit committee is evaluating the following risk matrix for a company:

|  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Item Number | Likelihood | Impact | Risk |
| 1 | 8.3% | $ 20,235 | Cash register embezzlement |
| 2 | 13.60% | 169,477 | Vendor kickbacks (collusion) |
| 3 | 7.5% | 522,531 | Server outage |
| 4 | 1.1% | 2,937,632 | Financial statement earning restatement |
question: Using statistical risk ranking methodology, which of the following lists of risks is correctly prioritized?

During the review of asset management procedures, an auditor in a large logistics firm determines that asset tracking systems are frequently bypassed, leading to inaccurate valuations. Which solution should the auditor propose to improve compliance with asset tracking protocols?

options.A: Conduct random audits to penalize noncompliance with asset tracking.
options.B: Integrate asset tracking with the ERP to automate updates and reconciliations.
options.C: Appoint a compliance officer to oversee adherence to asset tracking policies.
options.D: Increase physical security measures for high-value assets.

question: During a review of an organization’s asset management controls, an auditor finds that the fixed asset register has not been updated in over a year. What risk does this present to the business?

options.A: Overstated depreciation expenses.
options.B: Inaccurate reflection of asset use.
options.C: Improved long-term investment decisions.
options.D: Enhanced accuracy of inventory counts.

question: Company management completes event identification and analyzes the associated risks. The company wishes to assess its risk in the absence of any actions management might take to alter either the risk’s likelihood or impact. Which of the following types of risk does this situation represent?

options.A: Inherent risk.
options.B: Residual risk.
options.C: Event risk.
options.D: Economic risk.

question: Company management completes event identification and assesses the severity of risk. Management then acts to alter the severity of risk. Which of the following types of risk does this situation represent?

options.A: Inherent risk.
options.B: Actual residual risk.
options.C: Event risk.
options.D: Detection risk.

question: The process of assessing risks and controls in a business process is

options.A: Risk assessment.
options.B: Risk.
options.C: Risk matrix.
options.D: Risk monitoring.

question: Which one of the following is not considered a key step in the risk management process?

options.A: Prioritize risks.
options.B: Reconsider current risks.
options.C: Formulate risk responses.
options.D: Assess risks.

question: Risk is measured in terms of

options.A: Financial loss.
options.B: Risk appetite.
options.C: Safety value.
options.D: Probability and impact.

question: Risks are measured as the product of

options.A: Likelihood and duration.
options.B: Probability and impact.
options.C: Volatility and impact.
options.D: Volatility and duration.

question: The likelihood of achieving control objectives is affected by which limitation inherent to internal control?

options.A: The internal auditor’s primary responsibility is the detection of fraud.
options.B: Management assesses controls.
options.C: The cost of internal control should not exceed its benefits.
options.D: Management monitors internal control.

question: As part of an audit engagement, an internal auditor must assess whether the organization’s current risk assessment framework adequately covers new emerging risks identified by the market. What approach should the auditor take?

options.A: Use the organization’s historical risk data to predict future trends.
options.B: Interview frontline employees about their perspectives on emerging risks and compare with Topical Requirement guidelines.
options.C: Use a Topical Requirement to compare the framework with industry best practices and guidelines.
options.D: Assess legacy systems and IT controls for immediate vulnerabilities.

question: As part of an internal audit of regulatory compliance, auditors are required to understand and integrate Topical Requirements specific to third parties in the finance industry. What should the auditor prioritize to ensure compliance and enhance the effectiveness of the audit engagement?

options.A: Develop a risk heat map focused on internal process inefficiencies.
options.B: Regularly review The IIA’s Global Guidance documents for updates related to compliance and financial regulations.
options.C: Conduct interviews with financial analysts to gain insights into potential regulatory breaches.
options.D: Audit asset management risks during the audit engagement.

question: An internal auditor is assessing the risk management framework of a healthcare organization’s IT department after the recent implementation of new security protocols. Staff have conflicting opinions about their effectiveness. How should the auditor proceed to ensure that the protocols reflect industry best practices?

options.A: Ignore the staff’s concerns and rely on the department manager’s report.
options.B: Conduct an independent evaluation of the new protocols against recognized industry standards.
options.C: Suggest the department revert to the previous security protocols until all staff agree on the new ones.
options.D: Implement the new protocols and monitor their performance over the next 6 months before conducting a formal evaluation.

question: During an audit planning session, an internal auditor at a manufacturing company finds that quality management processes have not been reviewed against International Organization for Standardization (ISO) standards for over a year. options.D: Either a pre-printed ticket or a printout of an electronic ticket.

question: During an audit, information is uncovered that could have a significant impact on the organization’s competitiveness. According to IIA guidance, when is it appropriate for the internal auditor to communicate this information to management?

options.A: Immediately, because of the sensitivity of the information.
options.B: After the auditor has decided that the information is substantial and credible.
options.C: After the auditor has formulated recommendations.
options.D: As soon as the auditor has determined that communicating the information is not a violation of the organization’s code of conduct.

question: What characteristic of information is satisfied by an original signed document?

options.A: Sufficiency.
options.B: Reliability.
options.C: Relevance.
options.D: Usefulness.

question: An internal auditor has set an engagement objective of determining whether all cash receipts are deposited intact daily. To satisfy this objective, the internal auditor interviewed the controller who gave assurances that all cash receipts are deposited as soon as is reasonably possible. As information that can be used to satisfy the stated engagement objective, the controller’s assurances are

options.A: Sufficient but not reliable or relevant.
options.B: Sufficient, reliable, and relevant.
options.C: Not sufficient, reliable, or relevant.
options.D: Relevant but not sufficient or reliable.

question: In deciding whether recorded sales are valid, which of the following items of information is most reliable?

options.A: A copy of the customer’s purchase order.
options.B: A memorandum from the director of the shipping department stating that another employee verified the personal delivery of the merchandise to the customer.
options.C: Accounts receivable records showing cash collections from the customer.
options.D: The shipping document, independent bill of lading, and the invoice for the merchandise.

context:
The organization’s inventories are under the administration of three production managers. The internal auditors perform a standard limited test of finished goods inventory balances every year. During this year’s engagement concerning inventories, the internal auditors noted finished goods inventories were abnormally high, sales were consistent with prior years, and returns and allowances appeared normal. The internal auditors performed the usual random sample recount of several finished goods inventory cards without discrepancy and then extended the testing to include 10 raw materials and 10 work-in-process cards, noting no exceptions. The following statement was included in the engagement workpapers:

“Our standard test of finished goods inventories revealed no exceptions to the inventory count. We extended our tests this year to include both raw materials and work-in-process without exception. At the time of our engagement, the supervising inventory managers were not available; however, the division secretary indicated that performance standards were on file. It appears that there is adequate awareness and understanding of the performance standards.”
question: Which information criteria have been violated?

options.A: Sufficiency, only.
options.B: Reliability and sufficiency, only
options.C: Relevance and reliability, only.
options.D: Sufficiency, reliability, and relevance.

context: The organization is required to comply with certain specific standards related to environmental issues. One of these standards requires that certain hazardous chemicals be placed in certified containers for shipment to a governmental disposal site. The container must bear an inspection seal signed within the last 90 days by a governmental inspector. Based on the following tests, the internal auditor concluded that the organization was in compliance for the engagement period:
question: Which of the following informational criteria, if any, is violated?

options.A: Sufficiency.
options.B: Reliability.
options.C: Relevance.
options.D: No criteria are violated.

context: In an engagement to evaluate the effectiveness and validity of a subsidiary’s marketing expenditures, the internal auditors identified the following information:
question: Which of the following informational criteria, if any, is violated?

options.A: Sufficiency.
options.B: Reliability.
options.C: Relevance.
options.D: No criteria are violated.

context: In an engagement performed at the organization’s real estate development subsidiary, the engagement objective was to determine that capitalized land improvements had been assigned equally to all developed lots. The internal auditors identified the following information:
question: Which of the following informational criteria, if any, are violated?

options.A: Sufficiency and relevance.
options.B: Reliability and sufficiency.
options.C: Relevance and reliability.
options.D: No criteria are violated.

question: Management is investigating the acquisition of an upgraded version of the existing client-server system to increase the system’s capacity. Management has requested that the internal auditor perform an operational engagement to determine the efficiency of the existing computer processing resource. What is the most relevant source of information to meet the engagement objective?

options.A: A survey of current user satisfaction.
options.B: A review of computer job log records, listings of scheduled jobs, and computer down-time.
options.C: A comparison of server capacity with desktop computer capacity.
options.D: A detailed analysis of hard drive growth over the last 3 years.

question: The most reliable information an internal auditor can assess when determining an organization’s legal title to inventories is

options.A: Monthly gross profit and inventory levels.
options.B: Purchase orders.
options.C: Paid vendor invoices.
options.D: Records of inventories stored at off-site locations.

question: The reliability of information available to an internal auditor is least likely to be affected by the

options.A: Relevance of the information to the engagement objectives.
options.B: Relationship of the preparer of the information to the activity under review.
options.C: Timeliness of the information.
options.D: Sampling method employed to obtain a sample of the information.

question: Which of the following procedures would provide the most reliable information?

options.A: Inquiries of the organization’s employees held in private.
options.B: Inspection of prenumbered purchase orders filed in the vouchers payable department.
options.C: Analytical procedures performed by the internal auditor on the organization’s trial balance.
options.D: Inspection of bank statements obtained directly from the organization’s financial institution.

question: Which of the following presumptions relates more to the relevance of information than to its reliability?

options.A: The more effective internal control is, the more assurance it provides about the information.
options.B: An internal auditor’s conclusion is formed within a reasonable time to achieve a balance between benefit and cost.
options.C: Information obtained from independent sources outside the entity is more definitive than information secured solely within the entity.
options.D: The internal auditor’s direct personal knowledge obtained through observation is more persuasive than information obtained indirectly.

question: You have been assigned to an engagement involving the maintenance department. Which of the following is likely to produce the least reliable information?

options.A: Notes on discussions with mechanics in the maintenance operation.
options.B: A schedule comparing actual maintenance expenses with budgeted expenses and those of the prior period and disclosing important differences.
options.C: A narrative covering review of user reports on maintenance service.
options.D: An analysis of changes in certain maintenance department ratios.

question: An auditor finds discrepancies during an internal audit and has gathered testimonial evidence through interviews. What should the auditor do next to ensure the findings are reliable?

options.A: Conclude the audit and prepare the final report.
options.B: Obtain documentary evidence to corroborate interview findings.
options.C: Request an independent confirmation from a third party.
options.D: Undertake a statistical analysis of all obtained interview results.

question: An internal auditor suspects that the sales department has been overstating sales figures. Which of the following forms of evidence would be most relevant to support this suspicion?

options.A: Comparing sales records to shipping logs.
options.B: Interviewing the sales manager about sales practices.
options.C: Reviewing the sales department’s performance reports.
options.D: Observing the sales staff during meetings.

question: During an engagement, an internal auditor needs to establish that the information provided is both relevant and reliable. Which approach would best help the auditor in this task?

options.A: Reviewing corroborative documentary evidence obtained from internal sources over time.
options.B: Relying exclusively on system-generated reports verified by department heads.
options.C: Conducting unstructured interviews with key stakeholders to gain diverse perspectives.
options.D: Using data analytics to correlate information across different organizational inputs.

question: An internal auditor is asked to verify the reliability of information obtained from an internal audit. Which method is least likely to be effective in confirming reliability?

options.A: Corroborating the information with third-party records.
options.B: Confirming details through interviews with independent parties.
options.C: Reviewing the same information from independent system logs.
options.D: Accepting management’s explanations without verification.

question: Which situation best demonstrates the concept of sufficient information in an audit scenario involving a large retail chain?

options.A: Interviewing all store managers to gather direct insights on sales operations.
options.B: Auditing a representative sample of the stores’ sales records and projecting the findings.
options.C: Conducting a comprehensive audit of one major store only.
options.D: Reviewing historical trends in company-wide annual sales figures.

question: An internal auditor is tasked with evaluating the reliability of information obtained from a subsidiary’s sales department. Which of the following factors would strengthen the reliability of this information?

options.A: The information was obtained from internal reports prepared by the sales department.
options.B: The information was corroborated with data from independent market research.
options.C: The data were collected and verified more than 2 years ago.
options.D: The sales department manager vouched for the information’s accuracy.

question: In a financial services firm, the internal auditor is using data analysis to support findings related to transaction anomalies. What enhances the sufficiency of the data analyzed?

options.A: Using data from one specific department exclusively.
options.B: Relying on verbal confirmations from department heads.
options.C: Selecting samples using standard statistical methods.
options.D: Incorporating only the latest transaction entries for analysis.

question: While reviewing the internal control processes of a finance company, an auditor decides to evaluate the relevance of the data obtained. Which scenario best illustrates relevant data?

options.A: Documented proof of staff attendance at work.
options.B: Information on customers’ payment history related to credit assessment.
options.C: Historical data on finance industry trends.
options.D: Employee personal opinions on management policies.

question: An internal auditor conducting a risk assessment reviews information from the external email confirmations from suppliers and internal purchase orders. Which quality of information does this action primarily address?

options.A: Reliability.
options.B: Relevance.
options.C: Sufficient.
options.D: Independence.

question: Which scenario exemplifies the application of professional skepticism by an internal auditor during an audit?

options.A: Determining whether information is relevant to the objectives of the audit.
options.B: Scrutinizing evidence that appears inconsistent with initial findings.
options.C: Questioning the reliability of original corroborated information.
options.D: Performing a financial ratio trend analysis to assess the reasonableness of the gross profit margin.

question: When conducting an audit engagement, an internal auditor is evaluating the sufficiency of evidence collected. Which of the following best describes an audit scenario where evidence is likely considered sufficient?

options.A: Evidence gathered from third-party confirmations, direct observations, and reliable internal documents that align with audit objectives.
options.B: Evidence allows multiple interpretations, leading to varied conclusions among auditors.
options.C: Evidence is primarily based on the opinions and assertions provided by management without corroboration.
options.D: Evidence is obtained solely from data analyses performed without reviewing underlying documents.

question: An internal auditor is conducting an engagement at a mid-sized retail corporation and has gathered information through interviews with key personnel and observation of processes. What must the auditor do to enhance the reliability of the evidence gathered?

options.A: Cross-reference internal documents with observations made during walkthroughs.
options.B: Solely rely on testimonials from experienced employees.
options.C: Depend primarily on finalized internal control questionnaires.
options.D: Use statistical sampling methods to collect additional data.

question: Engagement information is usually considered relevant when it is

options.A: Derived through valid statistical sampling.
options.B: Objective and unbiased.
options.C: Factual, adequate, and convincing.
options.D: Consistent with the engagement objectives.

question: An internal auditor is reviewing documentation to assess compliance with company policies. What factor best determines the sufficiency of the evidence?

options.A: Whether the evidence aligns with management’s expectations.
options.B: Whether the evidence is convenient to obtain and easy to interpret.
options.C: Whether the evidence provides enough coverage to support audit conclusions.
options.D: Whether the evidence is appropriately documented and available for review in the audit file.

question: During an operational audit, an auditor gathers employee interviews and system-generated reports. What is the best way to assess the relevance of this evidence?

options.A: Determine whether you trust the employees interviewed and who provided the system data.
options.B: Determine whether the evidence is easy to capture and understand.
options.C: Determining whether the evidence directly relates to the audit objectives.
options.D: Determine whether the evidence is recent.

question: To verify the proper value of costs charged to real property records for improvements to the property, the best source of information is

options.A: Inspection by the internal auditor of real property improvements.
options.B: A letter signed by the real property manager asserting the propriety of costs incurred.
options.C: Original invoices supporting entries into the accounting records.
options.D: Comparison of billed amounts with contract estimates.

question: During interviews with the inventory management personnel, an internal auditor learned that salespersons often order inventory for stock without receiving the approval of the vice president of sales. Also, detail testing showed that there are no written approvals on purchase orders for replacement parts. The results of detail testing are a good example of

options.A: Indirect information.
options.B: Circumstantial information.
options.C: Corroborative information.
options.D: Subjective information.

question: The chief audit executive is reviewing the workpapers produced by an internal auditor during a fraud investigation. Among the items contained in the workpapers is a description of an item of physical information. Which of the following is the most probable source of this item of information?

options.A: Observing conditions.
options.B: Interviewing people.
options.C: Examining records.
options.D: Computing variances.

question: Which of the following techniques is most likely to result in sufficient information with regard to an engagement to review the quantity of fixed assets on hand in a particular department?

options.A: Physical observation.
options.B: Analytical review of purchase requests and subsequent invoices.
options.C: Interviews with department management.
options.D: Examination of the account balances contained in general and subsidiary ledgers.

question: Ordinarily, what source of information should most affect the internal auditor’s conclusions?

options.A: External.
options.B: Inquiry.
options.C: Oral.
options.D: Informal.

question: The most conclusive information to support supplier account balances is obtained by

options.A: Reviewing the vendor statements obtained from the accounts payable clerk.
options.B: Obtaining confirmations of balances from the suppliers.
options.C: Performing analytical account analysis.
options.D: Interviewing the accounts payable manager to determine the internal controls maintained over accounts payable processing.

question: An internal auditor’s objective is to determine the cause of inventory shortages shown by the physical inventories taken by an independent service organization that used some of the organization’s personnel. The internal auditor addresses this objective by reviewing the count sheets, inventory printouts, and memos from the last inventory. The source of information and the sufficiency of this information are

options.A: Internal and not sufficient.
options.B: External and sufficient.
options.C: Both external and internal and sufficient.
options.D: Both external and internal and not sufficient.

question: During an investigation of unexplained inventory shrinkage, an internal auditor is testing inventory additions as recorded in the perpetual inventory records. Because of internal control weaknesses, the information recorded on receiving reports may not be reliable. Under these circumstances, which of the following documents provides the best information about additions to inventory?

options.A: Purchase orders.
options.B: Purchase requisitions.
options.C: Vendors’ invoices.
options.D: Vendors’ statements.

question: In engagement planning, internal auditors should review all relevant information. Which of the following sources of information would most likely help identify suspected violations of environmental regulations?

options.A: Discussions with operating executives.
options.B: Review of trade publications.
options.C: Review of correspondence the organization has conducted with governmental agencies.
options.D: Discussions conducted with the external auditors in coordinating engagement efforts.

question: A letter to the internal auditor in response to an inquiry is an example of which type of information?

options.A: Physical.
options.B: Testimonial.
options.C: Documentary.
options.D: Analytical.

question: An internal auditor takes a photograph of the workplace for the activity under review. The photograph is a form of what kind of information?

options.A: Physical.
options.B: Testimonial.
options.C: Documentary.
options.D: Analytical.

question: Which of the following is an example of documentary information?

options.A: A photograph of the workplace of the activity under review.
options.B: A letter from a former employee alleging a fraud.
options.C: A page of the general ledger containing irregularities placed there by the perpetrator of a fraud.
options.D: A page of the internal auditor’s workpapers containing the computations that demonstrate the existence of an error or irregularity.

question: The internal auditor for a construction contractor finds materials costs increasing as a percentage of billings and suspects that materials billed to the organization are being delivered to another contractor. What type of information will best enable the internal auditor to determine whether erroneous billings occurred?

options.A: Documentary.
options.B: Physical examination.
options.C: Confirmation.
options.D: Analytical.

question: During an engagement to review the personnel function, an internal auditor notes that there are several employee benefit programs and that participation in some of the programs is optional. Which of the following is the best information for assessing the acceptability of various benefit programs to employees?

options.A: Discuss satisfaction levels with program participants.
options.B: Evaluate program participation ratios and their trends.
options.C: Discuss satisfaction levels with the director of personnel.
options.D: Evaluate methods used to make employees aware of available program options.

question: In an engagement to review travel expenses, the internal auditor calculates average expenses per day traveled for all sales personnel and then examines detailed receipts for those with high averages. These procedures represent the identification of which types of information?

options.A: Documentary and physical.
options.B: Analytical and physical.
options.C: Documentary and analytical.
options.D: Physical and testimonial.

question: An internal auditor arrived at the conclusion that the segregation of duties in the counting and recording of cash receipts was adequate. What type of information is this?

options.A: Analytical.
options.B: Documentary.
options.C: Physical.
options.D: Testimonial.

question: When evaluating the propriety of a payment to a consultant, the most appropriate information for the internal auditor to obtain and review is

options.A: Oral information in the form of opinions of operating management.
options.B: Documentary information in the form of a contract.
options.C: Analytical information in the form of comparisons with prior years’ expenditures on consultants.
options.D: Physical information in the form of the consultant’s report.

question: The most reliable forms of documentary evidence are those documents that are

options.A: Prenumbered.
options.B: Internally generated.
options.C: Easily duplicated.
options.D: Authorized by a responsible official.

question: Which of the following are least valuable in predicting the amount of uncollectible accounts for an organization?

options.A: Published economic indices indicating a general business downturn.
options.B: Dollar amounts of accounts actually written off by the organization for each of the past 6 months.
options.C: Total monthly sales for each of the past 6 months.
options.D: Written forecasts from the credit manager regarding expected future cash collections.

question: The most likely source of information indicating employee theft of inventory is

options.A: Physical inspection of the condition of inventory items on hand.
options.B: A warehouse employee’s verbal charge of theft.
options.C: Differences between an inventory count and perpetual inventory records.
options.D: Accounts payable transactions vouched to inventory receiving reports.

question: Which of the following types of tests is the most persuasive if an internal auditor wants assurance of the existence of inventory stored in a warehouse?

options.A: Examining the shipping documents that support recorded transfers to and from the warehouse.
options.B: Obtaining written confirmation from management.
options.C: Physically observing the inventory in the warehouse.
options.D: Examining warehouse receipts contained in the department’s records.

question: Documents provide information with differing degrees of persuasiveness. If the engagement objective is to obtain information that payment has actually been made for a specific invoice from a vendor, which of the following documents ordinarily is the most persuasive?

options.A: An entry in the cash disbursements journal supported by a voucher package containing the vendor’s invoice.
options.B: A canceled check, made out to the vendor and referenced to the invoice, included in a cutoff bank statement that the internal auditor received directly from the bank.
options.C: An accounts payable subsidiary ledger that shows payment of the invoice.
options.D: A vendor’s original invoice stamped “PAID” and referenced to a check number.

question: An internal auditor at a credit union concludes that a secured real estate loan is collectible. Which of the following engagement procedures provides the most persuasive information about the loan’s collectibility?

options.A: Confirming the loan balance with the borrower.
options.B: Reviewing the loan file for proper authorization by the credit committee.
options.C: Examining documentation of a recent, independent appraisal of the real estate.
options.D: Examining the loan application for appropriate borrowers’ signatures.

question: The most persuasive information regarding the asset value of newly acquired computers is

options.A: Inquiry of management.
options.B: Observation of the organization’s procedures.
options.C: Physical examination.
options.D: Documentation prepared externally.

question: The most persuasive information about the existence of newly acquired computers for the sales department is

options.A: Inquiry of management.
options.B: Observation of department procedures.
options.C: Physical examination.
options.D: Documentation prepared externally.

question: Which of the following represents the general order of persuasiveness, from most to least, for the types of information listed below? Inquiry of management Observation of operating procedures Physical examination Documentation prepared externally
The internal auditor wants to understand the actual flow of data regarding cash processing. The most convincing information is obtained by

options.A: Reviewing the systems flowchart.
options.B: Performing a walkthrough of the processing and obtaining copies of all documents used.
options.C: Reviewing the programming flowchart for information about control procedures placed into the computer programs.
options.D: Interviewing the chief financial officer.

question: The internal auditor is concerned with the overall valuation of inventory. Rank the following sources of engagement information from most persuasive to least persuasive in addressing the assertion as to the valuation of inventory. Calculate inventory turnover by individual product. Assess the net realizability of all inventory items with a turnover ratio of 2.0 or less by interviewing the marketing manager as to the marketability of the product. Calculate the net realizable value (NRV) of all inventory products (using software to calculate NRV based on the last selling price) and compare NRV with cost. Take a statistical sample of inventory and examine the latest purchase documents (invoices and receiving slips) to calculate inventory cost.
Which of the following examples of audit evidence is the most persuasive?

options.A: Real estate deeds that were properly recorded with a government agency.
options.B: Canceled checks written by the chief financial officer and returned from a bank.
options.C: Time cards for employees that are stored by a manager.
options.D: Vendor invoices filed by the accounting department.

question: One objective of an internal auditing engagement involving the receiving function is to determine whether receiving clerks independently count incoming supplies before completing the quantity received section of the receiving report. Which of the following is the most persuasive information supporting the assertion that the counts are made?

options.A: The receiving section supervisor’s assurance, based on personal observation, that the counts are made.
options.B: A receiving clerk’s initials on all receiving reports attesting that the count was made.
options.C: Assurance, from the warehouse supervisor, that the accuracy of the perpetual inventory is the result of the reliability of the entries in the quantity received section.
options.D: Periodic observations by the internal auditor over the course of the engagement.

question: An internal auditor is evaluating the advertising function. The organization has engaged a medium-sized local advertising agency to place advertising in magazine publications. As part of the review of the engagement workpapers, the internal auditing supervisor is evaluating the information collected. The internal auditor reviewed the language in the advertising for its legality and compliance with fair trade regulations by interviewing the organization’s advertising manager, the product marketing director (who may not have been objective), and five of the organization’s largest customers (who may not have been knowledgeable). The supervisor can justifiably conclude that the information is

options.A: Reliable.
options.B: Irrelevant.
options.C: Conclusive.
options.D: Insufficient.

question: In testing the write-off of a deteriorated piece of equipment, the best information about the condition of the equipment is

options.A: The equipment manager’s statement regarding condition.
options.B: Accounting records showing maintenance and repair costs.
options.C: A physical inspection of the actual piece of equipment.
options.D: The production department’s equipment downtime report.

question: Observation would provide insufficient audit evidence in which one of the following situations?

options.A: Verification of the existence of production equipment.
options.B: Documentation of a production or accounting process.
options.C: Analysis of the security of a storeroom or facility.
options.D: Identification of excess inventory.

question: Which of the following types of audit evidence is best defined as the proof of a fact without reliance on presumptions for support?

options.A: Direct.
options.B: Circumstantial.
options.C: Conclusive.
options.D: Corroborative.

question: In evaluating the evidence gathered during an audit, which characteristic is crucial to ensure the evidence can be relied upon for making conclusions?

options.A: Timeliness.
options.B: Consistency.
options.C: Tangibility.
options.D: Independence.

question: During an internal audit of a financial institution, the auditor must assess whether current lending practices comply with industry regulations. Which type of evidence should the auditor prioritize in this scenario?

options.A: Testimonial evidence from loan officers.
options.B: Analytical procedures comparing different fiscal quarters.
options.C: Documentary evidence of compliance checks and approvals.
options.D: Observations of daily lending operations.

question: During an internal audit engagement, an auditor needs to evaluate the reliability of the accounting software system in place at the organization. Which of the following actions would best achieve this objective?

options.A: Reviewing the system’s user manuals and documented guidelines.
options.B: Interviewing the IT manager about the system’s performance.
options.C: Observing the actual functioning of the software during operations.
options.D: Analyzing historical data processed by the system for accuracy and consistency.

question: During a fraud investigation, an internal auditor notices inconsistencies in employee time records. What should be the first step the auditor takes in gathering further evidence?

options.A: Interview an HR representative responsible for payroll.
options.B: Review relevant policies on time tracking and payroll procedures.
options.C: Conduct observations by visiting the department unannounced.
options.D: Analyze digital evidence such as system logs and audit trails.

question: An internal auditor is conducting a fraud risk assessment on the financial transactions of a large corporation. What is a critical step they should take when information provided by the company management appears incomplete?

options.A: Assume the information is complete as is customary practice, without inquiry.
options.B: Draft the findings based on the provided information regardless of its completeness.
options.C: Adjust the findings conservatively in the absence of complete information.
options.D: Perform further analysis and seek additional information to verify completeness.

question: A set of engagement workpapers contained a copy of a document providing information that an expensive item that had been special-ordered was actually on hand on a particular date. The most likely source of this information is a printout from a computerized

options.A: Purchases journal.
options.B: Cash payments journal.
options.C: Perpetual inventory file.
options.D: Receiving report file.

question: When auditing the inventory management process, an internal auditor observes conflicting information between the system records and physical counts. How should the auditor proceed?

options.A: Use the system records because they are regularly updated.
options.B: Initiate a thorough investigation to identify reasons for discrepancies.
options.C: Accept the physical counts as more reliable and adjust the records accordingly.
options.D: Conduct interviews to determine which records are correct.

question: Which of the following best describes how an auditor should handle incomplete information when concluding on the effectiveness of a process?

options.A: Proceed with conclusions using the information at hand.
options.B: Perform further analysis to assess implications of incomplete information.
options.C: Document a disclaimer regarding the reliability due to incomplete information.
options.D: Request additional information from the engagement organization and wait for it.

question: An auditor is verifying the effectiveness of a newly implemented control. What is the most appropriate way to evaluate the quality of evidence gathered?

options.A: Considering the experience of the staff interviewed who confirmed how the process operated.
options.B: Confirming that the evidence supports management’s position on the control.
options.C: Considering the age of the evidence–recent data is more reliable.
options.D: Ensuring the evidence is objective, complete, and obtained through reliable sources.

question: An auditor is verifying compliance with data privacy regulations. What type of evidence is most effective and would effectively allow another professional to reach the same conclusion?

options.A: A high-level summary of security policies.
options.B: A statement from IT management asserting compliance.
options.C: System access logs and documented data handling procedures.
options.D: A list of planned security improvements for future compliance efforts.

question: An audit team is evaluating expense reimbursements for fraud risk. What type of evidence would be most reliable and will allow another auditor to confirm the findings?

options.A: Original receipts, approval records, and transaction documentation.
options.B: Verbal explanations from employees about their expense claims.
options.C: A company policy stating reimbursement rules.
options.D: A memo from the finance department summarizing past reimbursements.

question: An auditor is assessing the effectiveness of internal controls over procurement. What type of evidence supports a strong conclusion and would allow another auditor to reach the same conclusion?

options.A: Records of conversations with employees about procurement practices employed.
options.B: Purchase orders, vendor contracts, and approval workflows.
options.C: Management’s assurance that procurement controls are being followed.
options.D: Published procurement process procedural documentation.

question: An internal audit report includes findings related to high-risk transactions. What type of evidence must be included to support a robust conclusion and ensure that another auditor could validate this?

options.A: Interview records from employees who processed high-risk transactions.
options.B: Detailed transaction records, supporting records, and audit trails.
options.C: A summary of past audits that previously identified similar risks.
options.D: An explanation from management about why the transactions occurred.

question: An auditor is testing controls over user access to critical IT systems. What evidence would support a robust conclusion to be drawn by another competent professional?

options.A: IT security policy acceptance records.
options.B: Verbal assurances from IT staff that access controls are enforced.
options.C: System access logs and user authorization records.
options.D: Employee feedback on their experiences with system access restrictions.

question: A well-designed internal control questionnaire should

options.A: Elicit “yes” or “no” responses rather than narrative responses and be organized by department.
options.B: Be a sufficient source of data for assessment of control risk.
options.C: Help evaluate the effectiveness of internal control.
options.D: Be independent of the objectives of the internal auditing engagement.

question: A questionnaire consists of a series of questions relating to controls normally required to prevent or detect errors and fraud that may occur for each type of transaction. Which of the following is a disadvantage of a questionnaire?

options.A: A questionnaire limits the scope of information sources and therefore risks the possibility of overlooking aspects of internal control.
options.B: A questionnaire is generally complicated and difficult to complete.
options.C: A questionnaire is inflexible in design and application.
options.D: The completed questionnaire has limited value as documentation and is generally not included in the workpapers.

question: An internal auditor is planning to conduct a survey to assess employee satisfaction with new compliance training. What should the auditor do when designing the survey to ensure maximum response rates and valuable insights?

options.A: Use technical jargon to demonstrate expertise.
options.B: Keep the questionnaire short and relevant to ensure engagement.
options.C: Focus solely on numeric scales for easy analysis.
options.D: Require names to hold respondents accountable for their feedback.

question: Fact Pattern: Management answered “yes” to every question when filling out an internal control questionnaire and stated that all listed requirements and control activities were part of their procedures. An internal auditor retrieved this questionnaire from management during the preliminary survey visit but did not review the responses with management while on site. The internal auditor’s supervisor should be critical of the above procedure because

options.A: Engagement information must be corroborated in some way.
options.B: Internal control questionnaires cannot be relied upon.
options.C: The internal auditors were not present while the questionnaire was being filled out.
options.D: The questionnaire was not designed to address accounting operations and controls.

question: Which of the following statements indicates the wrong way to use an internal control questionnaire?

options.A: Clarifying all answers with written remarks and explanations.
options.B: Filling out the questionnaire during an interview with the person who has responsibility for the activity under review.
