options.C: Constructing the questionnaire so that a “no” response requires attention.
options.D: Supplementing the completed questionnaire with a narrative description or flowchart.

question: An engagement supervisor is conducting the annual meeting with manufacturing division management to discuss proposed engagement plans and activities for the next year. After some discussion about the past year’s activity at 12 plants in the division, the divisional vice president agrees that all significant recommendations made by the engagement supervisor refer to key controls and related operating activities that are correctly described for local management within the volume of standard operating procedures for the division. The vice president proposes to transcribe key control activities from the division’s extensive written procedures to a self-assessment standard operating procedure (SOP) questionnaire. What significance should the engagement supervisor attach to such SOP questionnaires in relation to the proposed engagement schedule for the next year?

options.A: The SOP questionnaires should improve control adequacy, but the internal auditors need to verify that controls are working as documented in the SOP.
options.B: Adding this control should eliminate significant engagement recommendations in the coming year, so the scope of engagement activities can be reduced accordingly.
options.C: Engagement activity can be reduced if the vice president agrees to require the internal audit function’s approval of all divisional standard operating procedures.
options.D: SOP questionnaires must be mailed and controlled by the internal audit function to be considered in relation to the proposed engagement schedule.

question: An auditor is considering developing a questionnaire to research employee attitudes toward control procedures. All of the following are best-practice guidelines for designing questionnaires except

options.A: Questions must be worded to ensure a valid interpretation by the respondents.
options.B: Questions must be reliably worded so that they measure what was intended to be measured.
options.C: The questionnaire should be short to increase the response rate.
options.D: Personal questions should be asked first.

question: The auditor used a questionnaire during interviews to gather information about the nature of claims processing. Unfortunately, the questionnaire did not cover a number of pieces of information offered by the person being interviewed. Consequently, the auditor did not document the potential problems for further audit investigation. The primary deficiency with the process is that

options.A: The auditor failed to consider the importance of the information offered.
options.B: A questionnaire was used in a situation in which a structured interview should have been used.
options.C: Questionnaires do not allow for opportunities to document other information.
options.D: All of the answers are correct.

question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of transmitting an internal control questionnaire prior to an audit engagement?

options.A: Questionnaires add to the level of anxiety of managers of the function being audited.
options.B: The questionnaire helps the auditor but not the manager better understand the scope of the engagement.
options.C: Preparing the questionnaire is generally not cost effective.
options.D: The managers will respond only to the questions asked without volunteering additional information.

question: Which of the following statements describes an internal control questionnaire? It

options.A: Provides detailed evidence regarding the substance of the control system.
options.B: Takes less of management’s time to complete than other control evaluation devices.
options.C: Requires that the internal auditor be in attendance to properly administer it.
options.D: Provides indirect evidence that might need corroboration.

question: In an audit of a shipping department, the internal auditors conducted a survey to become familiar with its operations. The survey included interviewing key personnel using a formal questionnaire. The disadvantage of this procedure is that the interviewer

options.A: Is less likely to record information not specifically addressed in the questionnaire.
options.B: Is able to ask clarifying questions.
options.C: Is face-to-face with the interviewee.
options.D: May ask questions requiring an explanatory response.

question: How does the use of an internal control questionnaire assist an internal auditor in planning an engagement?

options.A: Increases apprehension for the employees of the activity under review.
options.B: Provides a complete understanding of unfamiliar and complex operations.
options.C: Information is gathered from those most familiar with it.
options.D: Decreases the uniformity of data acquisition.

question: Which of the following is an advantage of formal questionnaires properly prepared and transmitted in advance?

options.A: They are more effective than interviewing.
options.B: They are an opportunity for self-evaluation by operational management.
options.C: They eliminate the need for follow-up clarifying questions.
options.D: They address all circumstances.

question: Which approach should an internal auditor use to draft a questionnaire about internal control?

options.A: Wording so that a negative response indicates a problem.
options.B: Allowing responses only to questions asked prior to the engagement.
options.C: Measuring what was intended to be measured.
options.D: Flexibility in design and application.

question: Is Action 5 inappropriate?

options.A: Yes. Internal control should be evaluated on every engagement, but the internal control questionnaire is not the mandated approach to evaluate the controls.
options.B: No. Internal auditors may omit necessary procedures if there is a time constraint. It is a matter of professional judgment.
options.C: Yes. Internal control should be evaluated on every engagement, and the internal control questionnaire is the most efficient method to do so.
options.D: No. Internal auditors are not required to fill out internal control questionnaires on every engagement.

question: Many questionnaires are made up of a series of different questions that use the same response categories (e.g., strongly agree, agree, neither, disagree, strongly disagree). Some designs will have different groups of respondents answer alternative versions of the questionnaire that present the questions in different orders and reverse the orientation of the endpoints of the scale (e.g., agree on the right and disagree on the left or vice versa). The purpose of such questionnaire variations is to

options.A: Eliminate intentional misrepresentations.
options.B: Reduce the effects of pattern response tendencies.
options.C: Test whether respondents are reading the questionnaire.
options.D: Make it possible to get information about more than one population parameter using the same questions.

question: When preparing for an engagement, the internal auditor decides to use an internal control questionnaire. What is the main advantage of this tool?

options.A: It ensures the internal auditor can independently assess financial accuracy.
options.B: It encourages audit staff to become thoroughly familiar with the organization.
options.C: It systematically identifies control weaknesses for further investigation.
options.D: It reduces the need for detailed personal interviews.

question: An internal auditor is using an internal control questionnaire to assess the effectiveness of an organization’s procurement process. Which of the following should be included to ensure the questionnaire is effective?

options.A: Lengthy questions to ensure involvement.
options.B: A focus on routine processes rather than exceptions.
options.C: A “no” response flagging potential areas for further investigation.
options.D: Sole reliance on closed-ended questions.

question: In a healthcare organization, an auditor is using questionnaires to evaluate the effectiveness of patient data privacy controls. Which is the primary advantage of using questionnaires in this context?

options.A: They help involve staff in identifying potential issues through structured feedback.
options.B: They provide immediate solutions to identified weaknesses.
options.C: They are easily filled out without needing additional explanations.
options.D: They can replace all other forms of evidence collection.

question: An internal auditor plans to use an internal control questionnaire to assess an organization’s accounting department controls. Which of the following is a key advantage of using a questionnaire in this context?

options.A: It allows for flexibility in how questions are addressed.
options.B: It provides a qualitative measure of how each control operates.
options.C: It helps to identify all potential exceptions without requiring further follow-up.
options.D: It standardizes information gathering and facilitates the design of tests of controls.

question: Which of the following is most likely considered to determine whether internal controls are operating effectively?

options.A: A management representation letter corroborating inventory pricing.
options.B: A questionnaire completed by an employee in the receiving department about her duties and responsibilities.
options.C: Attorneys’ responses to an auditor’s inquiries.
options.D: Confirmations of receivables verifying account balances.

question: Which phrase best describes the control-based approach of the control self-assessment process?

options.A: Evaluating, updating, and streamlining selected control processes.
options.B: Examining how well controls are working in managing key risks.
options.C: Analyzing the gap between control design and control frameworks.
options.D: Determining the cost-effectiveness of controls.

question: Which forms of control self-assessment assume that managers and members of work teams possess an understanding of risk and control concepts and use those concepts in communications?

options.A: The self-certification approach.
options.B: The self-certification approach and facilitated approach.
options.C: The self-certification approach and questionnaire approach.
options.D: All self-assessment programs.

question: The aim of which format of the facilitated approach is to decide whether procedures are working effectively?

options.A: Control-based format.
options.B: Objective-based format.
options.C: Process-based format.
options.D: Risk-based format.

question: After reviewing the prior year’s internal audit recommendations, senior management has decided to adopt a control self-assessment (CSA) program using a questionnaire approach. The survey consists of descriptions of, and questions about, key controls. What is the effect on the next audit of adopting this CSA program?

options.A: Audit tests will be substantially eliminated.
options.B: The CSA survey must be controlled by the internal audit function.
options.C: The internal auditors need to verify that the controls are in place and working as intended.
options.D: The internal audit function will receive the results directly.

question: Why should an organization use the survey form of control self-assessment (CSA)?

options.A: Few respondents are required to respond.
options.B: Respondents are not widely dispersed.
options.C: No time constraint is involved.
options.D: The organizational culture does not encourage openness.

question: Of the three primary approaches of CSA programs, which one is designed to gather information from work teams representing different levels in the business unit or function?

options.A: Auditor-produced analysis.
options.B: Facilitated approach.
options.C: Questionnaire approach.
options.D: Self-certification approach.

question: Control self-assessment is a process that involves employees in assessing the adequacy of controls and identifying opportunities for improvement within an organization. Which of the following is a reason to involve employees in this process?

options.A: Employees are objective about their jobs.
options.B: Employees can provide an independent assessment of internal controls.
options.C: Employees become more motivated to do their jobs right.
options.D: Employees become more aware of the responsibility managers have for internal controls.

question: Which of the following statements about control self-assessment (CSA) is true?

options.A: CSA integrates business objectives, risks, and controls.
options.B: CSA is usually an informal and undocumented process.
options.C: CSA is also known as control and risk self-assessment but does not focus on risks.
options.D: Most implemented CSA programs are unique and do not share key features and goals.

question: Which group is charged with overseeing the establishment, administration, and evaluation of the processes of risk management and control?

options.A: Operating managers.
options.B: Internal auditors.
options.C: External auditors.
options.D: Senior management.

question: Which outcome can be derived from self-assessment methodologies?

options.A: Formal, hard controls are more easily identified and evaluated.
options.B: Management will become involved in and knowledgeable about the self-assessment process by serving as facilitators, scribes, and reporters for the work teams.
options.C: Auditors’ responsibility for the risk management and control processes of the organization will be reinforced.
options.D: People are motivated to take ownership of the control processes in their units and corrective actions taken by work teams are often more effective and timely.

question: Which type of facilitated approach format begins by listing all possible barriers, obstacles, threats, and exposures that might prevent achieving an objective?

options.A: Objective-based format.
options.B: Control-based format.
options.C: Process-based format.
options.D: Risk-based format.

question: The element(s) of a control self-assessment (CSA) performed using one of the facilitated team workshop approaches include(s)

options.A: Treating participating employees as process owners.
options.B: Taking a simple yes-or-no survey of employees regarding risks and controls.
options.C: Taking a simple yes-or-no survey of employees regarding risks and controls and interviewing employees separately in the field.
options.D: Treating participating employees as process owners and interviewing employees separately in the field.

question: In which format of the facilitated approach does the facilitator identify the key controls before the beginning of the workshop?

options.A: Control-based format.
options.B: Objective-based format.
options.C: Risk-based format.
options.D: Process-based format.

question: Which of the three primary approaches of CSA programs should be used if management wants to minimize the time spent and costs incurred in gathering the information?

options.A: Self-certification approach.
options.B: Facilitated approach.
options.C: Auditor-produced analysis.
options.D: Questionnaire approach.

question: Which one of the three primary types of CSA programs allows for the CAE to synthesize information provided by management with other information to enhance the understanding about controls and to share the knowledge?

options.A: Facilitated approach.
options.B: Self-certification approach.
options.C: Questionnaire approach.
options.D: Auditor-produced analysis.

question: Control self-assessment (CSA) is a method for examining and evaluating the organization’s system of control, which includes

options.A: Risk analysis.
options.B: Self-assessment approaches.
options.C: Traditional internal auditing concepts.
options.D: All of the answers are correct.

question: Which type of format of control self-assessment (CSA) facilitated approaches focuses on the best way to accomplish the goals of the organization?

options.A: Process-based format.
options.B: Control-based format.
options.C: Risk-based format.
options.D: Objective-based format.

question: Which of the following is the most important factor to consider when planning for a control self-assessment (CSA) workshop?

options.A: Voting technology.
options.B: Facilitation training.
options.C: Meeting location.
options.D: Survey question format.

question: Which of the following statements in regard to the approaches to a control self-assessment (CSA) program is correct?

options.A: The two approaches are facilitation and cost-benefit.
options.B: The two approaches are facilitation and self-certification.
options.C: The three approaches are facilitation, cost-benefit, and self-certification.
options.D: The three approaches are facilitation, survey, and self-certification.

question: While conducting a control self-assessment project in an IT division, an internal auditor asks managers to rate the severity of each identified risk and the strength of each related control. Which of the following represents the most significant disadvantage of this exercise?

options.A: Budget hours expended will exceed any tangible benefits.
options.B: Subsequent audits of the division may not be conducted.
options.C: Management may omit important control weaknesses.
options.D: The internal audit function will be viewed as responsible for controls.

question: When preparing an engagement work plan, an internal auditor must decide how to gather testimonial evidence efficiently. What method should be considered for this purpose?

options.A: Conducting individual interviews with each staff member.
options.B: Sending out a comprehensive survey to all employees.
options.C: Organizing focus groups with key personnel.
options.D: Reviewing existing documentation for testimonial insights.

question: The auditor conducted an interview with the manager. The auditor noted that the manager became uncomfortable and nervous, and changed the subject whenever the auditor raised questions about certain types of claims. The manager’s answers were consistent with company policies and procedures. When documenting the interview, the auditor should

options.A: Document the manager’s answers noting the nature of the nonverbal communications.
options.B: Not document the nonverbal communication because it is subjective and is not corroborated.
options.C: Conclude that the nonverbal communication is persuasive and that sufficient evidence exists to charge fraud against the group.
options.D: Ignore the specific answers given in the interview, because they are self-serving.

question: When conducting interviews during the early stages of an internal auditing engagement, it is more effective to

options.A: Ask for specific answers that can be quantified.
options.B: Ask people about their jobs.
options.C: Ask surprise questions about daily procedures.
options.D: Take advantage of the fear that is an important part of the engagement.

question: To elicit views on broad organizational risks and objectives from the board and senior management, an internal auditor should

options.A: List specific risk factors for consideration.
options.B: Develop spreadsheets with quantitative data relevant to the industry.
options.C: Use a nondirective approach to initiating discussion of mitigating risks.
options.D: Ask each member of management about specific risks listed in an industry reference.

question: Auditors must be effective listeners, especially when asking complex questions. To improve their listening, auditors should take care to do all the following except

options.A: Stop talking. It is very difficult to listen and talk at the same time.
options.B: Be patient. Allow the speaker ample time to respond.
options.C: Avoid all questions until the speaker has concluded.
options.D: Put the speaker at ease. A nervous speaker will be difficult to understand.

question: Listening effectiveness is best increased by

options.A: Resisting both internal and external distractions.
options.B: Waiting to review key concepts until the speaker is through talking.
options.C: Tuning out messages that do not seem to fit the meeting purpose.
options.D: Factoring in biases to evaluate the information being given.

question: An internal auditor is interviewing an employee. While listening to the interviewee, the internal auditor should

options.A: Prepare a response to the interviewee.
options.B: Take mental notes on the speaker’s nonverbal communication because it is more important than what is being said.
options.C: Make sure all details, as well as the main ideas of the interviewee, are remembered.
options.D: Integrate the incoming information from the interviewee with information that is already known.

question: A supportive behavior that a listener, such as an auditor or a supervisor, can use to encourage a speaker is to

options.A: Look away from the speaker to avoid any intimidation.
options.B: Interject a similar incident or experience.
options.C: Stop other activity or work while the person is talking.
options.D: Not respond verbally until the speaker stops talking.

question: When evaluating communication, the internal auditor should be aware that nonverbal communication

options.A: Is independent of a person’s cultural background.
options.B: Is often imprecise.
options.C: Always conveys a more truthful response than verbal communication.
options.D: Always conveys less information than verbal communication.

question: Internal auditors should be active listeners to gain the most information in an internal audit interview. Which of the following best describes how an active listener behaves in an interview? The listener

options.A: Judges and evaluates the information as it is presented.
options.B: Listens with acceptance, empathy, and intensity.
options.C: Avoids looking directly at the speaker and interrupting his or her train of thought.
options.D: Formulates arguments and conclusions as pieces of the speaker’s information fit together.

question: An internal auditor is using an internal control questionnaire as part of a preliminary survey. Which of the following is the best reason for the auditor to interview management regarding the questionnaire responses?

options.A: Interviews provide the opportunity to insert questions to probe promising areas.
options.B: Interviews are the most efficient way to upgrade the information to the level of objective evidence.
options.C: Interviewing is the least costly audit technique when a large amount of information is involved.
options.D: Interviewing is the only audit procedure that does not require confirmation of the information obtained.

question: During an interview with a data input clerk to discuss a computerized system used to track employee training requirements and compliance, an internal auditor identifies a potentially significant weakness in the system. The internal auditor should

options.A: Not mention the weakness, directly or indirectly, to avoid making the clerk uncomfortable.
options.B: Ask indirect questions that will help get more factual information relating to the potential weakness.
options.C: Ask the clerk about the weakness and determine immediately whether the observation should be communicated.
options.D: Conduct a second interview after determining whether the weakness actually exists.

question: During an interview to identify controls over the quality of wastewater discharge, the responsible employee refers only to a department procedure when asked about controls to ensure that samples are collected and analyzed. In the internal auditor’s experience, such operations should maintain a log to record all samples, the types of analyses performed, and whether results should be reported to management or regulatory agencies. For some reason, this employee is reluctant to discuss detailed responsibilities in this area. The best thing for the internal auditor to do in this case is

options.A: Continue the interview and discuss other elements of the employee’s duties, returning periodically to the samples and analytical results.
options.B: Relate what the internal auditor has seen at other facilities and tell the employee that the log is necessary.
options.C: Accept the information as given and record a finding that adequate controls are in place.
options.D: Interview the manager of the employee and discuss the employee’s duties in detail.

question: The current internal auditing engagement to evaluate disbursements activities shows a significant number of errors made during the accounts payable vouchering process that have resulted in lost discounts and an extraordinary number of adjustments and credit memos. Engagement hours are already over budget in this section because of the number of exceptions to be analyzed. Internal auditing staff has had time to observe the operations performed by each of the voucher clerks; sample and analyze transaction documents in the accounts payable, purchasing, and receiving departments; and obtain system statistics on transaction volume, error-correction transactions, and lost-discount summaries. To date, the causes for all types of errors noted during detail testing, observation, and analysis of exceptions have not been fully identified in any of the three departments. The most appropriate course of action for the engagement supervisor to determine the causes of these errors is to

options.A: Question and get the opinions of the accounts payable clerks and those involved in processing these transactions.
options.B: Expand sample sizes for attributes already tested in transactions entered by accounts payable, purchasing, and receiving.
options.C: Concentrate on engagement work program requirements for cash disbursements testing to discover any related information from those tests.
options.D: Describe the transaction-related problems identified to date in a special engagement communication to management without expressing a cause or an internal auditor’s conclusion about the situation.

question: As part of the test of the effectiveness of a disaster recovery plan, the auditor plans to interview five employees from each of five different departments (25 employees in all). After the first few interviews, what would be the best way for the auditor to remain attentive during the remaining interviews?

options.A: Make up completely different questions to stay interested.
options.B: Ask the questions in a slightly different format and in a different sequence.
options.C: Have the rest of the employees write down their responses.
options.D: Interview the remaining employees in groups of four or five.

question: Which of the following is most likely appropriate for an auditor conducting a preliminary survey interview?

options.A: Be aggressive because the interviewee must be made to realize the importance of the topic.
options.B: Use surprise interviewing as often as possible because an unsettled interviewee is less likely to deliver prepared answers.
options.C: Avoid being overly critical of the interviewee and his or her organizational unit.
options.D: Prepare questions beforehand and always make them broadly focused.

question: Fact Pattern: Management answered “yes” to every question when filling out an internal control questionnaire and stated that all listed requirements and control activities were part of their procedures. An internal auditor retrieved this questionnaire from management during the preliminary survey visit but did not review the responses with management while on site. The auditor’s supervisor is writing the performance assessment for the auditor on this preliminary survey assignment. The supervisor cites the need to review management’s responses on the control questionnaire. The auditor should have interviewed management for additional information because the interview technique

options.A: Provides the opportunity to insert questions to probe promising areas.
options.B: Is the most efficient way to upgrade the information to the level of objective evidence.
options.C: Is the least costly audit technique when a large amount of information is involved.
options.D: Is the only audit procedure that does not require confirmation and walkthrough of the information obtained.

question: Which of the following statements is true when comparing face-to-face interviews with written surveys?

options.A: The response rate for surveys is typically higher than for interviews.
options.B: Interviewers can increase a respondent’s comprehension of questions, which is not possible with formal written surveys.
options.C: Survey designers can use a wider variety of types of questions than can be used in interviews.
options.D: Surveys are more expensive than interviews.

question: During an interview, an internal auditor notices that the interviewee becomes defensive and less forthcoming. What should the auditor do to ensure effective information gathering?

options.A: Continue with the interview without addressing the interviewee’s defensiveness.
options.B: Terminate the interview and reschedule for another time.
options.C: Assume the defensiveness indicates wrongdoing and focus questions accordingly.
options.D: Reassure the interviewee and explain the value of his or her input.

question: When preparing to conduct interviews at a technology company, an internal auditor decides to use open-ended questions during interviews as an initial approach. What is the primary benefit of this approach?

options.A: It saves time by limiting responses to “yes” or “no” answers.
options.B: It allows interviewees to express themselves comprehensively, leading to unexpected insights.
options.C: It makes it easier to compare responses across different interviewees.
options.D: It helps to maintain control over the interview content.

question: During an internal audit engagement in a manufacturing company, the internal auditor encounters resistance from employees who are unsure why certain data are being collected. How should the auditor address this concern?

options.A: Provide a comprehensive explanation of the engagement objectives and how employee input is valuable.
options.B: Avoid informing the employees about the purpose of the data collection.
options.C: Demand cooperation because it is part of the audit process.
options.D: Collect data without interacting further with resistant employees.

question: When conducting an interview, an auditor finds that the interviewee is becoming defensive. What is the best course of action for the auditor to take?

options.A: Ask direct questions to put the interviewee at ease.
options.B: Study body language to determine why the interviewee is becoming defensive.
options.C: Pause and reassure the interviewee of the interview’s purpose.
options.D: Conclude the interview to avoid further resistance.

question: Tolerating silence, asking open-ended questions, and paraphrasing are three aids to more effective

options.A: Meetings.
options.B: Listening.
options.C: Interviews.
options.D: Feedback.

question: When an internal auditor is interviewing to gain information, (s)he will not be able to remember everything that was said in the interview. The most effective way to record interview information for later use is to

options.A: Write notes quickly, trying to write down everything in detail as it is said; then highlight important points after the meeting.
options.B: Digitally record the interview to document everything that everyone says.
options.C: Hire a professional secretary to take notes, allowing complete concentration on the interview; then delete unimportant points after the meeting.
options.D: Organize notes around topics on the interview plan and note responses in the appropriate area, reviewing the notes after the meeting to make additions.

question: As part of an engagement to evaluate safety management programs, an internal auditor interviews the individual responsible for writing, issuing, and maintaining safety procedures. While the internal auditor’s primary interest is to identify the controls ensuring that procedures are kept current, the individual has a tremendous amount of information and seems intent on telling the internal auditor most of it. What might the internal auditor do to guard against missing what is important?

options.A: Write down everything the individual says. If the internal auditor gets behind, ask for a pause and catch up. After the interview, the internal auditor can sift through the notes and be confident of finding the key information.
options.B: Record the interview and later extract the relevant information.
options.C: Do not sort through extraneous information. Revisit the topic with the individual’s supervisor and obtain any needed information at that time.
options.D: During the conversation, make an effort to anticipate the approach of a point of critical interest.

question: How should an auditor ensure the accuracy of the conclusions derived from interviews with staff members?

options.A: Conduct surprise interviews with staff who were not previously interviewed to verify information reported.
options.B: Use AI to analyze the text of the interviews to identify inconsistencies.
options.C: Conduct a thorough review of documentation and corroborating evidence alongside interview responses.
options.D: Use only the interview feedback for drafting the conclusion.

question: Which of the following procedures is the internal auditor most likely to perform at the beginning of an engagement?

options.A: Prepare a rough draft of the report.
options.B: Evaluate the adequacy and effectiveness of controls.
options.C: Tour the facilities for the activity under review.
options.D: Consult with and review the work of the predecessor internal auditor.

question: An internal auditor wishes to evaluate the design of and perform procedures on controls over cash disbursements procedures. If the controls leave no audit trail of documentary evidence, the internal auditor most likely will test the procedures by

options.A: Confirmation and observation.
options.B: Observation and inquiry.
options.C: Analytical procedures and confirmation.
options.D: Inquiry and analytical procedures.

question: Observation is considered a reliable procedure but one that is limited in usefulness. However, it is used in a number of different situations. Which of the following statements is true regarding observation?

options.A: It is the most effective method to use in filling out internal control questionnaires.
options.B: It is the most persuasive method to learn how transactions are really processed during the period under audit.
options.C: It is most persuasive about the performance of a process but is limited to the moment in time at which the observation takes place.
options.D: It is the most persuasive procedure for determining whether fraud has occurred.

question: An internal auditor must weigh the cost of an engagement procedure against the persuasiveness of the evidence to be gathered. Observation is one engagement procedure that involves cost-benefit trade-offs. Which of the following statements regarding observation as an engagement technique is true?

options.A: Observation is effective in identifying employees’ feelings about their work.
options.B: Observation is more persuasive for the completeness assertion than it is for the existence assertion.
options.C: Observation is limited because individuals may react differently when being observed.
options.D: Observation involves following transactions through a process to understand how transactions are initiated, authorized, processed, and recorded.

question: Nonresponse bias is often a concern in conducting written surveys. The main reason that nonresponse bias can cause difficulties in a sample such as the one taken by the customer service office is that

options.A: The sample means and standard errors are harder to compute.
options.B: Those who did not respond may be systematically different from those who did.
options.C: The questionnaire is too short.
options.D: Confidence intervals are narrower.

question: Several of the internal auditing team members are concerned about the low response rate, the poor quality of the questionnaire design, and the potentially biased wording of some of the questions. They suggest that the customer service office might want to supplement the survey with some unobtrusive data collection such as observing customer interactions in the office or collecting audios of phone conversations with customers. All of the following are potential advantages of unobtrusive data collection compared to surveys or interviews except

options.A: Interactions with customers can be observed as they occur in their natural setting.
options.B: It is easier to make precise measurements of the variables under study.
options.C: Unexpected or unusual events are more likely to be observed.
options.D: People are less likely to alter their behavior because they are being studied.

question: An internal auditing team developed a preliminary questionnaire with the following response choices: Probably not a problem Possibly a problem Probably a problem The questionnaire illustrates the use of

options.A: Trend analysis.
options.B: Ratio analysis.
options.C: Unobtrusive measures or observations.
options.D: Rating scales.

question: An insurance company has received many complaints from customers about long turnaround times for claims submitted and errors in processing claims. Which of the following procedures is the least effective in gathering information about the nature of the processing of claims and potential problems?

options.A: Interview supervisors in the claims department to find out more about the procedures used, and the rationale for the procedures, and obtain their observations about the nature and efficiency of processing.
options.B: Send an email to all clerical personnel detailing the alleged problems and request their input.
options.C: Interview selected clerical employees in the claims department to find out more about the procedures used, and the rationale for the procedures, and obtain their observations about the nature and efficiency of processing.
options.D: Distribute a questionnaire to gain a greater understanding of the responsibilities for claims processing and the control procedures utilized.

question: The annual physical inventory of the main warehouse was recorded by existing surveillance cameras. The cameras were unobtrusive and the employees had long forgotten of their existence. Unable to attend the actual physical inventory, the audit manager observed the video footage. What advantage did the auditor gain by observing the recorded video inventory over observing in person?

options.A: The recorded version is more persuasive for the occurrence assertion.
options.B: The auditor can determine whether written policies have been implemented.
options.C: Employee behavior was not influenced by observation.
options.D: Private behavior, feelings, and motives can be better observed using the recorded version.

question: An organization has continual large shortages at the cash registers despite having procedures in place. A local accounting firm was retained to audit the organization’s control procedures over cash. Several types of audit procedures were used during the engagement. Which of the following is the best example of the data-gathering method of observation?

options.A: Upon examination of cash register tapes, the auditor discovered cash drawers were opened several times during employee shifts with no corresponding sales.
options.B: The auditor spoke with several employees, including the store manager, about the steps they follow when voiding a sales transaction.
options.C: Reconciliations of cash deposits with sales records were performed by the auditor.
options.D: The auditor watched one of the morning shift employees pay the delivery driver out of the cash register.

question: All of the following are limitations of observation as an information gathering method except

options.A: It has a slow response time.
options.B: It lacks measurement precision.
options.C: It is less persuasive for the completeness assertion.
options.D: Certain attributes cannot be observed.

question: The dean at a prestigious private performing arts college was reading about the 20 amazing students graduating with honors in the spring. The dean wants to gather the following information from the students’ families: Why did the students choose this college? How did the students go through the decision-making process? What method would the college’s audit supervisor most likely suggest for gathering this information?

options.A: Sending a questionnaire to the students’ families.
options.B: Interviewing the students’ families via telephone.
options.C: Having the students complete a rating scale survey.
options.D: Observing the activities of the students.

question: Which of the following procedures most likely provides an internal auditor with the most assurance about the effectiveness of the operation of a control?

options.A: Inquiry of operational personnel.
options.B: Recomputation of account balance amounts.
options.C: Observation of operational personnel.
options.D: Confirmation with outside parties.

question: While observing a warehouse operation, an auditor notes that employees are not following the documented procedures for inventory counts. What immediate action should the auditor take?

options.A: Report the issue to senior management immediately.
options.B: Confront the employees about their deviation from procedures.
options.C: Observe for a longer period to determine if noncompliance is widespread.
options.D: Collect documentary evidence of the observed procedures.

question: An auditor encounters a department using outdated procedures not documented in the current SOPs during a walkthrough. What is the best course of action?

options.A: Document the finding and proceed without further discussion.
options.B: Recommend immediate suspension of the outdated procedures.
options.C: Discuss the issue with the department head to update SOPs and align practices.
options.D: Assume the outdated procedures are sufficient due to lack of complaints.

question: In a logistical corporation, an auditor observes the loading and unloading procedures at a warehouse. What is the primary limitation of using observation in this context?

options.A: It confirms the occurrence but not the completeness of transactions.
options.B: Observation introduces bias due to auditor’s presence.
options.C: It relies on indirect information for conclusions.
options.D: Observers cannot document their findings simultaneously.

question: In documenting the procedures used by several interacting departments the internal auditor will most likely use a(n)

options.A: Horizontal (or systems) flowchart.
options.B: Vertical flowchart.
options.C: Gantt chart.
options.D: Internal control questionnaire.

question: Which of the following best describes the purpose of the cylindrical symbol on a flowchart?

options.A: Storage.
options.B: Computer operations.
options.C: Input or output used.
options.D: Connect points on the same page.

question: Which of the following tools would best give a graphical representation of a sequence of activities and decisions?

options.A: Flowchart.
options.B: Control chart.
options.C: Histogram.
options.D: Run chart.

question: The normal sequence of documents and operations on a well-prepared systems flowchart is

options.A: Top to bottom and left to right.
options.B: Bottom to top and left to right.
options.C: Top to bottom and right to left.
options.D: Bottom to top and right to left.

question: An auditor frequently uses flowcharts to determine whether there is

options.A: Satisfactory performance of an operation.
options.B: Sufficient but not excessive personnel assigned to an operation.
options.C: Authority to meet the performance criteria.
options.D: Inefficiency and lack of controls.

question: An internal auditor reviews and adapts a systems flowchart to understand the flow of information in the processing of cash receipts. Which of the following statements is true regarding the use of such flowcharts? The flowcharts

options.A: Show specific control procedures used, such as edit tests that are implemented and batch control reconciliations.
options.B: Are a good guide to potential segregation of duties.
options.C: Are generally kept up to date for systems changes.
options.D: Show only computer processing, not manual processing.

question: The diamond-shaped symbol is commonly used in flowcharting to show or represent a(n)

options.A: Process or a single step in a procedure or program.
options.B: Manual file.
options.C: Decision point, conditional testing, or branching.
options.D: Input.

options.B: images/u11_q8_5_15.png
options.C: images/u11_q8_5_16.png
options.D: images/u11_q8_5_17.png

question: When documenting internal control, the independent auditor sometimes uses a systems flowchart, which can best be described as a

options.A: Pictorial presentation of the flow of instructions in an internal computer system.
options.B: Diagram that clearly indicates an organization’s internal reporting structure.
options.C: Graphic illustration of the flow of operations that is used to replace the auditor’s internal control questionnaire.
options.D: Symbolic representation of a system or series of sequential processes.

question: Of the following, which is the most efficient source for an auditor to use to evaluate an organization’s overall control system?

options.A: Control flowcharts.
options.B: Copies of standard operating procedures.
options.C: A narrative describing departmental history, activities, and forms usage.
options.D: Copies of industry operating standards.

question: An auditor’s flowchart of an organization’s accounting system is a diagrammatic representation that depicts the auditor’s

options.A: Assessment of the risks of material misstatement.
options.B: Identification of weaknesses in the system.
options.C: Assessment of the control environment’s effectiveness.
options.D: Understanding of the system.

question: Which method of evaluating internal controls during the preliminary survey provides the internal auditor with the best visual grasp of a system and a means for analyzing complex operations?

options.A: A flowcharting approach.
options.B: A questionnaire approach.
options.C: A matrix approach.
options.D: A detailed narrative approach.

question: Internal auditors often flowchart a control system and reference the flowchart to narrative descriptions of certain activities. This is an appropriate procedure to

options.A: Determine whether the system meets established management objectives.
options.B: Document that the system meets international auditing requirements.
options.C: Determine whether the system can be relied upon to produce accurate information.
options.D: Gain the understanding necessary to test the effectiveness of the system.

question: An internal auditor develops a flowchart primarily to

options.A: Detect errors and irregularities.
options.B: Analyze a system and identify internal controls.
options.C: Determine functional responsibilities.
options.D: Reduce the need for interviewing operational personnel.

question: A flowchart of process activities and controls may provide

options.A: Information on where fraud could occur.
options.B: Information on the extent of a past fraud.
options.C: An indication of where fraud has occurred in a process.
options.D: No information related to fraud prevention.

question: The internal auditor wishes to develop a flowchart of (1) the process of receiving sales order information at headquarters, (2) the transmission of the data to the plants to generate the shipment, and (3) the plants’ processing of the information for shipment. The internal auditor should

options.A: Start with management’s decisions to set sales prices. Gather internal documentation on the approval process for changing sales prices. Complement documentation with a copy of the program flowchart. Prepare an overview flowchart that links these details.
options.B: Start with a shipment of goods and trace the transaction back through the origination of the sales order as received from the sales representative.
options.C: Start with the receipt of a sales order from a sales representative and “walk through” both the manual and computerized processing at headquarters and the plant until the goods are shipped and billed.
options.D: Obtain a copy of the plants’ systems flowchart for the sales process, interview relevant personnel to determine if any changes have been made, and then develop an overview flowchart which will highlight the basic process.

question: Graphical notations that show the flow and transformation of data within a system or business area are called

options.A: Action diagrams.
options.B: Program structure charts.
options.C: Conceptual data models.
options.D: Data flow diagrams.

question: Which of the following is a true statement comparing a horizontal flowchart with a vertical flowchart?

options.A: A horizontal flowchart provides more room for written descriptions that parallel the symbols.
options.B: A horizontal flowchart brings into sharper focus the assignment of duties and independent checks on performance.
options.C: A horizontal flowchart is usually longer.
options.D: A horizontal flowchart does not provide as broad a picture at a glance.

question:
The following is a section of a system flowchart for a payroll application:

Symbol X could represent

options.A: Erroneous time cards.
options.B: An error report.
options.C: Batched time cards.
options.D: Unclaimed payroll checks.

question: An advantage of using systems flowcharts to document information about internal control instead of using internal control questionnaires is that systems flowcharts

options.A: Identify internal control deficiencies more prominently.
options.B: Provide a visual depiction of the process under review.
options.C: Indicate whether controls are operating effectively.
options.D: Reduce the need to observe employee performance of routine tasks.

question: Which of the following is optimal to provide a summary-level description of a complex new computer system?

options.A: A control flowchart.
options.B: Program code checking and flowchart verification.
options.C: A system flowchart.
options.D: A detailed narrative.

question: Which of the following is true of analytical approaches and process mapping?

options.A: RACI diagrams are ineffective for cross-functional processes.
options.B: Only data flow diagrams apply to computerized systems.
options.C: Auditors use flowcharts at the end of an audit to verify the processes and controls of the activity under review.
options.D: Data flow diagrams have no symbols for output.

question: The correct labeling, in order, for the following flowchart symbols is

options.A: Document, display, online storage, and entry operation.
options.B: Manual operation, processing, offline storage, and input-output activity.
options.C: Display, document, online storage, and entry operation.
options.D: Manual operation, document, online storage, and entry operation.

question: The graphic portrayal of the flow of data and the information processing of a system, including computer hardware, is best displayed in a

options.A: Data-flow diagram.
options.B: System flowchart.

options.D: Program flowchart.

question:
In connection with the consideration of internal control, an auditor encounters the following flowcharting symbols:

The auditor should conclude that a

options.A: Master file has been created by a manual operation.
options.B: Master file has been created by a computer operation.
options.C: Document has been generated by a computer operation.
options.D: Document has been generated by a manual operation.

question: An internal auditor in the healthcare sector needs to evaluate the effectiveness of internal controls in the patient billing process. Which tool would allow the auditor to map the end-to-end process and identify control gaps?

options.A: A responsibility assignment matrix.
options.B: A vertical flowchart.
options.C: A spaghetti map.
options.D: A data flow diagram.

question: An internal auditor is evaluating the effectiveness of controls in a manufacturing company’s inventory process. The company uses a vertical flowchart layout with many interdepartmental transactions. Which feature should the auditor focus on to ensure a comprehensive review?

options.A: The swim lanes dividing departmental responsibilities.
options.B: The color coding of different departments.
options.C: The size of flowchart symbols.
options.D: The linearity of flowchart paths.

question: An internal auditor is using process mapping to analyze a bank’s loan approval process. What step should the auditor undertake to ensure an accurate understanding of the process?

options.A: Rely on automated tools to gather data for the process map.
options.B: Conduct a walkthrough of the process to directly observe each step involved.
options.C: Create a flowchart based on industry-standard practices without consulting bank personnel.
options.D: Simplify the process map to focus on decision-making steps.

question: An internal auditor is assessing the efficiency of the accounts payable process in a large manufacturing company. During the evaluation, the auditor decides to use a flowchart to map out the process. Which of the following is a primary benefit of using flowcharting in this scenario?

options.A: Flowcharts automatically improve process efficiency by identifying errors.
options.B: Flowcharts allow for the simplification of the approval process by bypassing non-essential steps.
options.C: Flowcharts visually represent the process, making it easier to identify gaps or redundancies in controls.
options.D: Flowcharts guarantee the elimination of fraud within the process.

question: During an internal audit engagement at XYZ Corporation, an internal auditor discovered a flowchart lacking clear indication of data flow between departments, leading to difficulties in identifying control weaknesses. How should the auditor address this issue?

options.A: Ignore the missing data flow and proceed with existing information.
options.B: Create a timeline-based narrative to supplement the flowchart.
options.C: Focus solely on financial data because they provide enough insights.
options.D: Develop a detailed process map that includes missing data flows.

question: While conducting an internal audit at a healthcare organization, an auditor is tasked with documenting procedures using a narrative form instead of a flowchart. What might be an advantage of using narratives over flowcharts in this setting?

options.A: Narratives can provide more detailed context, especially in complex processes within healthcare.
options.B: Narratives are generally easier to understand than flowcharts.
options.C: Narratives eliminate the need for audits.
options.D: Narratives can be created without any input from operational personnel.

question: An internal auditor is using a RACI diagram to evaluate a complex project. What is the primary benefit of this tool for the auditor?

options.A: To help predict the project’s success based on historical data.
options.B: To provide insights into the costs associated with the project.
options.C: To clarify roles and responsibilities, aiding in accountability assessment.
options.D: To outline the chronological steps required to complete the project.

question: An internal auditor is performing a review of an organization’s procurement process by using flowcharting. Which deficiency would indicate a potential risk of misappropriation of funds during this process?

options.A: Absence of segregation of duties between ordering and receiving functions.
options.B: Lack of a standard operating procedure for procurement.
options.C: Infrequent updates to a vendor master list.
options.D: Manual recordkeeping of purchase receipts.

question: During an audit of a mid-sized manufacturing company, the internal auditor encounters a spaghetti map that suggests significant inefficiencies in the material supply process. What would be an appropriate response by the auditor?

options.A: Recommend that the supply chain manager implement full automation of the current process.
options.B: Document the finding and proceed with the engagement without taking further action.
options.C: Prepare a set of financial ratios to determine if the inefficiencies are affecting financial results.
options.D: Suggest operations staff conduct a detailed review to streamline processes.

question: A financial services organization is implementing a new data analytics tool for audit purposes. As an internal auditor, which initial step should be taken to ensure effective implementation?

options.A: Conduct a walkthrough of the current data processes.
options.B: Develop a comprehensive benchmark against industry data.
options.C: Deploy the tool across multiple departments immediately.
options.D: Schedule frequent training sessions with the audit team.

question: An internal auditor is mapping a company’s procurement process. What is the first step in defining workflow segments?

options.A: Reviewing holistic data on procurement activity undertaken during the most recent financial year.
options.B: Interviewing employees about their personal experiences with procurement.
options.C: Analyzing previous audit reports on procurement inefficiencies.
options.D: Identifying key activities and decision points in the process.

question: A company is implementing automation in its accounts payable process. What is the first step in defining workflow segments for automation?

options.A: Reviewing existing automated practices to see what is currently successful.
options.B: Mapping manual steps such as invoice receipt, approval, and payment processing.
options.C: Asking employees for opinions on areas to be automated.
options.D: Benchmarking existing practices with competitor processes.

question: During an audit of the accounts payable process, an auditor performs a walk-through. What is the main purpose of this technique?

options.A: To test the knowledge of the operational team and assess their performance.
options.B: Observing and documenting the process flow to validate actual execution.
options.C: To build empathy with management of the activity under review.
options.D: To demonstrate compliance with the Internal Audit manual.

question: A company is mapping its payroll workflow and wants to clarify roles and responsibilities. Which tool would be most effective?

options.A: A workflow timeline that identifies key processing stages and assigned roles.
options.B: A company policy document specifying payroll procedures and approval workflows.
options.C: A payroll transaction log that includes details of assigned responsibilities.
options.D: A responsibility assignment matrix to define roles and accountability.

question: A manufacturing company wants to ensure clear accountability in its inventory control workflow. What method should be used?

options.A: Benchmarking control workflows to those operated by competitors.
options.B: Surveying employees to understand their job responsibilities.
options.C: Requesting line managers reiterate roles as per job descriptions.
options.D: Creating a responsibility assignment matrix to define tasks and ownership.

question: An internal audit team is performing a walk-through of the cash disbursement process. What is the key benefit of this approach?

options.A: Doubling as training for an auditor for future roles.
options.B: Saving on detailed testing if time is short.
options.C: Enabling rapport and relationships to be built with operational management.
options.D: Identifying process gaps by directly following transactions from initiation to completion.

question: Internal auditors must base conclusions on

options.A: Appropriate analyses.
options.B: Findings.
options.C: Recommendations.
options.D: Reports.

question: A small city managed its own pension fund. According to the city charter, investments could be made only in bonds, money market funds, or high-quality stocks. The internal auditor has already verified the existence of the pension fund’s assets. The fund balance was not very large and was managed by the city’s CFO. The internal auditor decided to estimate income from investments of the fund by multiplying the average fund balance by a weighted-average rate based on the current portfolio mix. Upon doing so, the internal auditor found that recorded return was substantially less than was expected. The internal auditor’s next procedure should be to

options.A: Inquire of the CFO as to the reason that income appears to be less than expected.
options.B: Prepare a more detailed estimate of income by consulting a dividend and reporting service that lists the interest or dividends paid on specific stocks and bonds.
options.C: Inform management and the board that fraud is suspected and suggest that legal counsel be called in to complete the investigation.
options.D: Select a sample of entries to the pension fund income account and trace it to the cash journal to determine if cash was received.

question: Analytical procedures

options.A: Are considered direct information about the assertion being evaluated.
options.B: Involve such tests as confirmation of receivables.
options.C: Provide the best available information for the completeness assertion.
options.D: Are never sufficient by themselves to support management assertions.

question: During an operational audit engagement, an auditor compared the inventory turnover rate of a subsidiary with established industry standards in order to

options.A: Evaluate the accuracy of internal financial reports.
options.B: Test controls designed to safeguard assets.
options.C: Determine compliance with corporate procedures regarding inventory levels.
options.D: Assess performance and indicate where additional audit work may be needed.

question: An organization’s primary focus is on what it needs to do in order to accomplish its predicted future. Which of the following data analytics methods would best address this concern?

options.A: Predictive analysis.
options.B: Prescriptive analysis.
options.C: Anomaly detection.
options.D: Network analysis.

question: The internal auditor wishes to assess the effects of advertising expense on sales of fall merchandise. Which of the following is the most appropriate procedure?

options.A: Regression analysis of the advertising budget in relation to sales for the most recent fall quarter.
options.B: Examination of customer surveys for comments in relation to the new ad campaign.
options.C: Comparison of same-store sales for the most recent fall quarter and previous fall quarters.
options.D: Trend analysis of sales for the previous year.

question: Accounts payable schedule verification may include the use of analytical information. Which of the following is analytical information?

options.A: Comparing the schedule with the accounts payable ledger or unpaid voucher file.
options.B: Comparing the balance on the schedule with the balances of prior years.
options.C: Comparing confirmations received from selected creditors with the accounts payable ledger.
options.D: Examining vendors’ invoices in support of selected items on the schedule.

question: During an engagement, the internal auditor should consider the following factor(s) in determining the extent to which analytical procedures should be used during the engagement:

options.A: Adequacy of the system of internal control.
options.B: Significance of the activity under review.
options.C: Precision with which the results of analytical audit procedures can be predicted.
options.D: All of the answers are correct.

question: The internal auditor of an organization with a recently automated human resources system reviews the retirement benefits plan and determines that the pension and medical benefits have been changed several times in the past 10 years. The internal auditor wishes to determine whether further investigation is justified. The most appropriate engagement procedure is to

options.A: Review the trend of overall retirement expense over the last 10 years. If it has increased, further investigation is needed.
options.B: Use generalized audit software to take a monetary-unit sample of retirement pay and determine whether each retired employee was paid correctly.
options.C: Review reasonableness of retirement pay and medical expenses on a per-person basis stratified by which plan was in effect when the employee retired.
options.D: Use generalized audit software to take an attribute sample of retirement pay and perform detailed testing to determine whether each person chosen was given the proper benefits.

question: Which of the following is an analytical procedure used by internal auditors?

options.A: Tracing transactions through the system to determine whether procedures are being applied as prescribed.
options.B: Comparing financial data with data for comparable prior periods, forecasts, and similar data for the industry in which the organization operates.
options.C: Creating a diagram that represents a process.
options.D: Creating a matrix that is used to clarify decision-making assignments in cross-functional or departmental projects and processes.

question: Analytical procedures in which current financial statements are compared with budgets or previous statements are primarily intended to determine the

options.A: Adequacy of financial statement disclosure.
options.B: Existence of specific errors or omissions.
options.C: Overall reasonableness of statement contents.
options.D: Use of an erroneous cutoff date.

question: A rental car organization’s fleet maintenance division uses a different code for each type of inventory transaction. A daily summary report lists activity by part number and transaction code. The report is reconciled by the parts room supervisor to the day’s material request forms and is then forwarded to the fleet manager for approval. The use of transaction codes provides the fleet manager with information concerning the types of inventory activities. The internal auditor is considering an analytical review of transaction codes and materials used. The objective of this review is to

options.A: Provide information about overstocked inventory items.
options.B: Reveal shortages in perpetual inventory records.
options.C: Determine whether inventory items are properly valued.
options.D: Identify possible material lost due to employee theft.

question: In which of the following situations is the use of an analytical review to verify the correctness of various operating expenses the least effective?

options.A: An auditor notes strong indicators of a specific fraud involving these accounts.
options.B: Operations are relatively stable and have not changed much over the past year.
options.C: An auditor would like to identify large, unusual, or non-recurring transactions during the year.
options.D: Operating expenses vary in relation to other operating expenses, but not in relation to revenue.

question: A government auditor was assigned to determine reasons why the students in one region scored significantly higher on education evaluation tests than the students in another region. Previous research showed that there is a direct correlation between public financial support and student results. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for the difference in regional results?

options.A: The more successful region spends 30 percent more money on education than does the other region.
options.B: A higher percentage of the general tax funds is spent on education in the more successful region than in the other region.
options.C: The more successful region spends more money per student on education than does the other region.
options.D: The more successful region has increased educational spending by an average of 10 percent each year for the last three years, whereas the other region’s increase averaged only 3 percent.

question: An inexperienced internal auditor notified the senior auditor of a significant variance from the organization’s budget. The senior told the new internal auditor not to worry because the senior auditor had heard that there had been an unauthorized work stoppage that probably accounted for the difference. Which of the following statements is most appropriate?

options.A: The new internal auditor should have investigated the matter fully and not bothered the senior auditor.
options.B: The senior auditor used proper judgment in curtailing what could have been a wasteful investigation.
options.C: The senior auditor should have halted the engagement until the variance was fully explained.
options.D: The senior auditor should have aided the new internal auditor in formulating a plan for accumulating appropriate information.

question: While testing the effectiveness of inventory controls, the internal auditor makes a note in the workpapers that most of the cycle count adjustments for the facility involved transactions of the machining department. The machining department also had generated an extraordinary number of cycle count adjustments in comparison with other departments last year. The internal auditor should

options.A: Interview management and apply other engagement procedures to determine whether transaction controls and procedures within the machining department are adequate.
options.B: Do no further work because the concern was not identified by the analytical procedures included in the engagement work program.
options.C: Notify the CAE that fraud is suspected.
options.D: Place a note in the workpapers to review this matter in detail during the next engagement.

question: An internal auditor was evaluating the effectiveness and efficiency of an organization’s motor pool, which is a centralized system for employees to use and share motor vehicles. The engagement work program included the use of analytical procedures to observe the trend of expenses for major overhauls of heavy-wheeled vehicles. This trend showed a substantial increase in the last year of the ratios of monetary amounts spent in relation to (1) the number of vehicles being used, (2) the mileage of the vehicles, (3) the age of the equipment, and (4) environmental conditions. The auditor’s investigation indicated that two new maintenance firms were being used. The expenditure packages from the maintenance work were complete; however, the billings for the work had an unusual regularity. The identification of the vehicles being serviced did not correspond to the vehicle maintenance reports. Possible engagement procedures include

The data reveal that three stores in Organization A are characterized by significantly lower gross margins, higher-than-average sales volume, and higher levels of employee bonuses. question: Which of the following tasks can be achieved using generalized audit software?

options.A: Determining acceptable risk levels for substantive testing of account balances.
options.B: Filtering data based on accounts receivable data recording.
options.C: Detecting transactions that may be suspicious due to alteration of data input.
options.D: Assessing likelihood of fraud based on input of fraud risk factors.

question: The results of a generalized audit software simulation of the aging of accounts receivable revealed substantial differences in the aging distribution, even though grand totals reconciled. Which of the following should the auditor do first to resolve the discrepancy?

options.A: Recreate the test, using different software.
options.B: List a sample of actual data to verify the accuracy of the test program.
options.C: Ignore the discrepancy because the grand totals reconcile and instruct the controller to correct the program.
options.D: Create test transactions and run test data on both the production and simulation programs.

question: Which of the following statements is true of the test data approach to testing an accounting system?

options.A: Test data are processed by the organization’s programs under the computer operator’s control.
options.B: The test data need consist of only those valid and invalid conditions that interest the auditor.
options.C: Only one transaction of each type can be tested.
options.D: The test data must consist of all possible valid and invalid conditions.

question: In parallel simulation, actual data from the department under review are reprocessed using an auditor software program. An advantage of using parallel simulation, instead of performing tests of controls manually, is that

options.A: The test includes all types of transaction errors and exceptions that may be encountered.
options.B: The department’s personnel do not know when the data are being tested.
options.C: There is no risk of creating potentially material errors in the department’s data.
options.D: The size of the sample can be greatly expanded at relatively little additional cost.

options.A:
Tests of Controls

Yes

No

Tests of Controls
